### CLAUDE (2026-07-07T17:35:11.633Z)

**953 rows** written to `apps/route-planner-v2/public/data/vehicles_femsa.csv`, headers matching the existing `vehicles.csv` so the app's import flow can consume it without a new mapper.

**Field derivation**

| Column | Source |
|---|---|
| `id` | Zone name — `{vehicleId}-{week}-{day}` (e.g. `1-1-Mon`) |
| `start_latitude/longitude` | Solution route's `steps[type=start].location` |
| `end_latitude/longitude` | Solution route's `steps[type=end].location` |
| `date` | `steps[type=start].arrival` in São Paulo local time, as `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| `shift_start_local` / `shift_end_local` | Start/end step `arrival` in SP local time, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` |
| `max_working_time_seconds` | `end.arrival − start.arrival` (actual duration of the solved shift) |
| `capacity` | `200` (same value we used as `max_cluster_quantity` earlier) |
| `zones` | The zone id assigned to this route in `input_femsa.json` |
| `name`, `telephone`, `home_address`, `break_*` | Left blank — no data for these in the JSON |

Every row's start and end lat/lng is the same `-23.504659,-46.562973` point — the single depot for the whole fleet. Shift starts uniformly at 08:00 local; ends vary by route (16:53–16:59 in the first few rows, matching the ~9-hour service days).

**Trade-offs worth naming**
- `capacity: 200` is a nominal value; if you want the actual per-route job count as capacity (so each vehicle is sized to what it delivered), that's a one-line change.
- `max_working_time_seconds` reflects the *solved* shift length, not a policy cap. If you want a policy cap (e.g. `32400` = 9 hours) that lets a re-run stretch the day, say the word and I'll swap it.
- The `zones` column contains a single zone id per row (the route-day zone). If you want a **fleet-wide allowed-zones list** instead (every vehicle able to visit any zone) so a re-optimization can shuffle assignments, that's also a small change — the current shape locks each vehicle to its original route.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-09T13:30:45.532Z)

Reload FEMSA2. Pick any route from the list and its zone(s) should now render.

**Root cause**
FEMSA2's zones are `{id, geometry}` — no `name` field. My earlier gate regex-parsed `zone.name` for a leading `{vehicleId}-` (the naming convention we baked into FEMSA1), so with no name every zone was filtered out even after selecting a route.

**Fix**
Zone visibility is now driven by the actual `job.zones` assignments in `rawInput.jobs`, not by name parsing:

1. Build `jobId → Set<zoneId>` from `rawInput.jobs`.
2. For each selected route, walk its `type='job'` steps, look up each job's zones, and union them into `touchedZoneIds`.
3. Filter `rawInput.zones` down to `touchedZoneIds`.

Comparisons go through `String(...)` on both sides so this works for FEMSA1 (jobs stamped with `zones: ["3"]` strings) and FEMSA2 (`zones: [3]` numbers). The "narrowed selection = show detail; all-selected or empty = hide" gate is unchanged.

The naming convention isn't required by any consumer now, so we're free to drop it in future zone-building scripts if we want.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-09T13:42:00.451Z)

Reload FEMSA1 or FEMSA2 — the routes tab now has a **Filter by zone** multi-select under the From/To datetime row.

**Behavior**
- Options come from `_rawInput.zones` (labelled by `zone.name`, or `Zone <id>` when unnamed), sorted by numeric id.
- Pick one or more → routes are filtered to those whose job steps land in any of the picked zones (union, not intersection). The auto-select effect then narrows the route selection to the visible subset, which in turn:
  - lights up the polylines for those routes (subset selection unhides them),
  - lights up the zone polygons for the selected zones (the zones layer's job-driven filter maps back).
- Empty selection → no zone filter applied. Clearing selection via the input's `×` also removes the filter without touching manual route picks.
- **Cross-filter with search + time range**: all three predicates are ANDed. Search finds a job substring, time range clips by route activity window, and zones require any-of-picked-zones membership — great for slicing "Monday of week 2, `VEND. TRADICIONAL` jobs, in zones 4–6".

Panel only appears when the loaded solution actually has zone geometries (`_rawInput.zones` has at least one entry with `.geometry`). So for the imported flow or a plain GCS solution without zones, the filter row is hidden — no dead UI.

Files changed:
- `v3/stores/ui.store.ts` — added `selectedZoneIds: string[]` state + `setSelectedZoneIds` action.
- `v3/features/solution/components/result-panel.tsx` — new `RouteZoneFilter` sub-component (MUI `Autocomplete<ZoneFilterOption, true>` with Chip tags), `jobIdToZoneIds` memo, zone predicate added to `filteredRoutes`, `selectedZoneIds` added to the auto-select `useEffect` deps + gate, `hasZones` gate for rendering.
- Five locale files — added `zoneFilterLabel` / `zoneFilterPlaceholder` / `zoneFilterEmpty` under the `solution` namespace (English, Portuguese-BR, Spanish-MX, French-CA, Polish).

### CLAUDE (2026-07-10T12:50:04.022Z)

Here's what I found. tl;dr: three surgical changes plus one bonus — imported-solution editing has the same bug and would get fixed for free.

## What already works

Drag/drop editing operates purely on an in-memory `draft` in `route-edit.store.ts`. `moveStepCrossRoute`, `moveUnassignedToRoute`, `bulkMove*` never call the network beyond `directionsApi.getDirections` (schedule recompute). Fine for fixtures.

## What breaks for FEMSA1/FEMSA2

**1. The "Edit route" button auto-saves before entering edit mode**
`solution-toolbar.tsx:481` gates on `source === 'db'`; for anything else it calls `handleAutoSave()` first, which posts `solutionFoldersApi.saveSolution({request_id: 'FEMSA1'})` to Waymer's `POST /solutions:save`. FEMSA1 isn't a real request → 404, save-to-folder dialog opens, user never enters edit mode. **The imported flow (`_import`) has the same bug** — that path was never actually working end-to-end.

**2. Apply (Confirm changes) 404s on GCS**
`route-edit.store.ts:892-963` branches by source:
- `'db'` → `solutionFoldersApi.editRoutes` (Waymer)
- `'imported'` → `updateImportedSolutionResult` (localStorage) ← the working template
- else (`'gcs'` for fixtures) → `optimizationApi.editRoutesGcs` → `POST optimization/v2/edit_routes` → 404

**3. Reload wipes edits**
`use-solution-data.ts:145` always refetches `femsa1_response.json` on mount. Any persisted edit is thrown away unless the fixture branch reads from a local slot first.

Changes complete. Reload FEMSA1 or FEMSA2 → click **Edit route** → make a drag-drop move → **Apply** → refresh the page. The edited state now survives.

## Summary of changes

**`v3/domain/types/optimization.ts`**
- `SolutionSource` `'imported'` → `'local'`. Docstring updated to name both local-mode sub-flows.

**`v3/stores/solution.store.ts`**
- New requestId-keyed helpers `saveLocalSolution` / `updateLocalSolutionResult` / `loadLocalSolution` / `loadLocalInput` / `clearLocalSolution`.
- Legacy single-slot key names (`rp:imported-solution` / `rp:imported-input`) preserved for `IMPORTED_REQUEST_ID`, so existing imported data in users' browsers still hydrates.
- Named fixtures (FEMSA1/FEMSA2/etc.) get their own `rp:local-solution:{id}` / `rp:local-input:{id}` slots.
- Backwards-compat aliases (`saveImportedSolution`, etc.) delegate to the new helpers with `IMPORTED_REQUEST_ID` — so `raw-json-panel.tsx` is untouched.
- `autoSave` early-returns for `source === 'local'` as defense in depth.

**`v3/features/solution/hooks/use-solution-data.ts`**
- Imported branch now sets `source: 'local'` (was `'imported'`).
- Two hard-coded FEMSA branches collapsed into a single `FIXTURES` map + one shared branch. New request IDs just need an entry in `FIXTURES` — no code changes.
- Fixture branch checks `loadLocalSolution(requestId)` and `loadLocalInput(requestId)` FIRST. If either is present, the local override is used; otherwise it fetches the bundled JSON. That's the piece that makes edits survive reload.
- Both local branches unified on `loadLocalSolution(requestId)` — the `_import` sentinel still routes to the legacy keys via the store helper.

**`v3/stores/route-edit.store.ts`**
- Apply's `source === 'imported'` branch → `source === 'local'`, and calls `updateLocalSolutionResult(requestId, ...)` instead of the single-slot legacy helper. `_import` and `FEMSA*` share the same code path, keyed by requestId.

**`v3/features/solution/components/solution-toolbar.tsx`**
- New `isLocalSource` derived from `useSolutionStore((s) => s.source === 'local')` — subsumes the `isImported` requestId check.
- `handleEditRoute` and `handleShare` skip the `handleAutoSave()` handshake for `source === 'local'` (was only skipping for `'db'`). This is the bug fix that unblocked editing for both imported and fixture solutions — previously both went straight to `saveSolution(...)` and hit a 404.
- `canSave` / `canShare` gate off `isLocalSource` instead of `isImported` — so save-to-folder and share buttons hide for both flavors.
- `isImported` variable retained (used by the request-id text-input placeholder) but is now a superset case of `isLocalSource`.

## What this unlocks
- Editing works end-to-end for FEMSA1, FEMSA2, and any future fixture you add to the `FIXTURES` map.
- Imported-JSON editing (previously broken because the toolbar tried to save before entering edit mode) now works too — bonus fix.
- Bundled fixtures are never mutated on disk; edits live in localStorage keyed per request id.

## Not yet done (from the "one detail" I asked about earlier)
No "Reset to original" affordance yet — right now the only way to clear a local override is DevTools → Application → Local Storage → delete the `rp:local-solution:FEMSA1` (or `-input:`) key. If you want a small toolbar button that calls `clearLocalSolution(requestId)` + `reload()`, say the word and I'll add it (single button, ~15 LOC, visible only when `isLocalSource && !isEditing`).

### CLAUDE (2026-07-11T13:52:42.588Z)

Three deploy paths for this repo. All start from your feature branch `feat/route-planner-v2-misc-enhancements`.

## 1. PR preview (best for showing FEMSA changes without merging)

Auto-triggers when a PR is open. If you haven't opened one yet:

```bash
git status                    # confirm nothing sensitive is staged
git push -u origin feat/route-planner-v2-misc-enhancements
gh pr create --base main --title "route-planner-v2 FEMSA fixtures + edit flow"
```

The `preview-deploy.yml` workflow will build the affected apps (route-planner-v2 will be one of them since we touched it heavily), push Docker images to GCR, and post a comment on the PR with URLs like:

```
https://console-preview-route-planner-v2-pr<N>-<hash>-uc.a.run.app/route-planner
```

Auto-teardown on PR close/merge.

**Local variant** (skip PR, deploy directly from your machine):

```bash
gcloud auth login             # if not already authenticated
yarn preview:deploy route-planner-v2 femsa-demo
# → https://console-preview-route-planner-v2-femsa-demo-<hash>-uc.a.run.app/route-planner

# When done:
yarn preview:teardown route-planner-v2 femsa-demo
```

Uses `.env.preview`; project = `nextbillion`, region = `asia-southeast1`. Docs: `docs/09 - preview deployments.md:80-140`.

## 2. Staging (auto, on merge to main)

Once the PR is reviewed and merged into `main`, `.github/workflows/main.yml` builds nx-affected apps, uploads to the staging GCS CDN + artifact bucket, and deploys to Cloud Run staging. No manual action from you.

## 3. Production (tagged release from main)

**Rule from `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`**: I won't tag, push, or publish a release without your explicit go-ahead — and neither will the release scripts (they all default to `--dry-run`; you have to pass `--execute`).

Once the change is on main and staging looks good, run these from repo root — **read the dry-run output before adding `--execute`**:

```bash
# Sanity check first (exit 1 = hard fail, 2 = warnings)
./tools/release/release-preflight.sh

# Compute what the next tag should be (reads latest v1.3.N tag)
./tools/release/next-version.sh

# See what the release notes would look like
./tools/release/generate-notes.sh

# The one command that actually cuts the release. Dry-run by default:
./tools/release/create-github-release.sh
# ...check output, then:
./tools/release/create-github-release.sh --execute
```

`create-github-release.sh --execute` tags the SHA on main with `v1.3.N`, publishes a GitHub Release, and triggers `.github/workflows/release.yml` which builds and deploys each affected app to prod Cloud Run. It also watches the workflow run to completion.

Docs: `.cursor/skills/ncc-release/SKILL.md` (the canonical playbook) and `docs/11-single-branch-release-flow.md`.

## Gotchas worth knowing before you release

- **`gh` must be authenticated** — orphan-tag logic in `release-preflight.sh` breaks with partial GitHub visibility. `gh auth status` first.
- **Substring matcher in `release.yml`**: `route-planner` is a substring of `route-planner-v2`. That's handled with a `&& !contains(name, 'route-planner-v2')` guard for the v2 case, but the `route-planner-viewer` overlap is **not**. If `nx affected` picks up `route-planner-viewer` for your release but not the legacy `route-planner`, the legacy prod deploy will still fire. Rare, but flagged in `CLAUDE.md`.
- **Hotfix invariant**: if a prior hotfix tag hasn't been back-merged into main, preflight hard-fails. Don't override with `--allow-orphan-tags`.

## Which path do you want?

- **Just want to eyeball the FEMSA fixtures on a live URL?** → PR preview (#1). Cheapest, fastest, no risk to staging/prod.
- **Ready to ship the FEMSA + edit-flow work to staging?** → Merge the PR, staging auto-deploys.
- **Ready for prod?** → Tell me when staging is verified and I'll walk you through `#3` step by step (still won't `--execute` without your explicit OK per each command).

## Before you run

Your working tree has substantial uncommitted work from this session (the FEMSA fixtures, edit flow, zone/time/search filters, i18n additions). Docker will build from your working tree, so **all of it will be in the shipped bundle** — but the image tag will use the current git SHA, which won't reflect that. Two options:

- **A** (recommended): commit first so the SHA tag matches what's actually built.
- **B**: tag manually with something like `femsa-demo-2026-07-11` so you don't confuse an old SHA with a new bundle.

Speak up if you want me to help stage/commit the changes first — otherwise these instructions assume Option B.

## Deploy

Run from **monorepo root** (Nx needs the full workspace for the standalone bundle).

**1. Configure Docker to push to Artifact Registry**
```bash
gcloud auth configure-docker us-central1-docker.pkg.dev
```

**2. Pick a tag and build the image**
```bash
# Option A (committed): use the commit SHA
TAG=$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)

# Option B (dirty tree): a descriptive manual tag
TAG=femsa-demo-$(date +%Y%m%d)

### CLAUDE (2026-07-11T15:15:18.408Z)

Cloud Run pulls `version = "latest"`, so adding a new secret version is enough — no redeploy needed. Here's the sequence:

## 1. Mint a fresh staging NCC token

Log into the staging console and grab a new token. The one you used before was from `iam-stg.nextbillion.ai`. If you have the token from a fresh browser session, drop it in a file so we don't pass it as a shell argument (avoids leaking it into your zsh history):

```bash
# Paste the new JWT into this file — nothing else
$EDITOR /tmp/ncc_token.txt
```

## 2. Push it as a new secret version

The secret name Cloud Run reads is `[REDACTED_SECRET]` in project `[GCP_PROJECT]`.

```bash
gcloud secrets versions add [REDACTED_SECRET] \
  --project=[GCP_PROJECT] \
  --data-file=/tmp/ncc_token.txt
```

Confirm it landed:
```bash
gcloud secrets versions list [REDACTED_SECRET] \
  --project=[GCP_PROJECT] --limit=3
```

Then wipe the file: `rm /tmp/ncc_token.txt`.

## 3. Force Cloud Run to pick up the new "latest"

Cloud Run only re-reads secrets when a new revision starts. Bounce the current revision by adding a no-op annotation so a fresh revision spins up with the new secret version:

```bash
gcloud run services update route-planner-v2-staging \
  --project=[GCP_PROJECT] \
  --region=us-central1 \
  --update-labels="secret-rotated-at=$(date +%s)"
```

Then hit the app, hit `/dev-login`, and confirm the new token cookie is being issued.

Alternative if you're already redeploying with terraform for other reasons: `terraform apply` will roll a fresh revision as a side effect and skip the labels-update step.

Returns the day\n * integer when the name parses, else null (e.g. numeric zone ids for\n * FEMSA2 fall through and skip day filtering).\n */\nfunction parseZoneDayOfWeek(zoneName: string | undefined): number | null {\n  if (!zoneName) return null\n  const m = /^Zone-\\d+-(\\d+)-\\d+$/i.exec(zoneName)\n  if (!m) return null\n  const d = Number.parseInt(m[1], 10)\n  return d >= 1 && d <= 7 ? d : null\n}\n\n/**\n * Day-of-week (Sunday=1..Saturday=7) for an epoch-seconds timestamp,\n * evaluated in `timezone` when provided so the boundary matches the\n * date label the UI shows for the same step.\n */\nfunction dayOfWeekFromArrival(arrival: number, timezone?: string): number {\n  const d = timezone ? dayjs.unix(arrival).tz(timezone) : dayjs.unix(arrival)\n  return d.day() + 1\n}"

### CLAUDE (2026-07-13T12:34:35.026Z)

No errors in the files I touched. Summary:

**Fix in place**: zone filter now combines two constraints:
1. **Primary-zone match** — a route is included only when its most-visited zone is in the selected set (drops routes with just a few stragglers).

### CLAUDE (2026-07-13T14:35:17.839Z)

Rep filter is in place. Behavior:

- **Options**: derived from `route.description`, stripped of the `-{week}-{day}` suffix (regex `-\d+-\d+$`), deduped, sorted. For FEMSA1 that's 100 rep names (A.Araujo, A.Fernandes, …).
- **Filter**: multi-select — a route survives when its stripped description matches one of the selected reps. Combines with the zone/time/search filters via AND (each further narrows).
- **Auto-select**: same behavior as the other filters — flipping the selection auto-checks the matching route rows.
- **UI gate**: the filter box now appears when the solution has zones OR descriptions, and both filters stack in it.
- **i18n**: `repFilterLabel/Placeholder/Empty` translated across en / pt-BR / es-MX / fr-CA / pl-PL.

Reload and you'll see "Filter by rep" under the zone filter. Picking, say, `B.Pereira` will narrow to that rep's routes across all shifts.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-13T14:45:57.247Z)

Clean. What was happening:

- `pctChange(288.13, 300.23)` returned `-4`.
- `isUp = pct > 0` → `false` (correct: value went down).
- `isGood = !isUp` → `true` (correct: distance dropped, that's good).
- **But** the icon selector was `{isGood ? TrendUp : TrendDown}` — a favorable change always drew an up arrow, even when the underlying number went down. That's the "increase of 4%" misread.

After the fix:
- Arrow direction = **direction of change** (`isUp`) — value went down → down arrow.
- Arrow + text color = **favorability** (`isGood`) — a distance decrease renders **green**, so you get a green down arrow next to green "4%".

So the same 300.23 → 288.13 edit will now display as `↘ 4%` in green.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-13T15:00:17.220Z)

The 23% jump isn't a UI bug — it's a **model mismatch** between what produced the baseline and what recomputes the draft.

**Baseline** (300.23 km / 306 min / cost 18383):
- Comes from the optimizer's response `route.duration` and `route.cost`.
- Optimizer computed cost from its precomputed cost matrix (whatever backend produced FEMSA1's solution). `travel_cost: "duration"` means cost = optimizer-modeled travel duration.

**Draft** (290.24 km / 377 min / cost 22671):
- Distance & duration recomputed by `applyDirectionsResult` calling the **NB Directions API** with the trimmed waypoints (see `route-edit.store.ts:604` → `buildDirectionsQuery` → `directions.api.ts`).
- Cost is then `Math.round(route.duration)` (since `travel_cost = duration`) — that's why cost and time move together identically at 23%.

So distance behaves as expected (–3% for two dropped stops), but the duration Directions returns can diverge from what the optimizer used. Two known reasons:

1. **`departure_time` gets sent** (`recalculate-route.ts:42`):
   ```ts
   departure_time: route.steps.at(0)?.arrival
   ```
   NB Directions applies traffic prediction based on that time. If the optimizer's cost matrix was traffic-free, Directions can easily add 15–25% for a peak-hour departure — hence "shorter route, longer time".

2. **Different routing engines** — the optimizer's cost matrix and the live Directions engine don't share weights. Two calls for the same waypoints won't match to the digit.

The fix if you want the delta to look sane on this demo: drop `departure_time` from the Directions query so it stops factoring traffic. That gives an apples-to-apples comparison against the optimizer's traffic-free matrix. Downside — you lose the traffic-aware ETA everywhere Directions is called during edit.

Want me to strip `departure_time` from `buildDirectionsQuery`? Or leave it and treat the delta panel as "predicted real-world ETA vs. optimizer's model" (which is arguably more honest)?

### CLAUDE (2026-07-13T15:08:54.517Z)

Clean. Two changes in one:

1. **Nothing new persists.** `partialize` now returns `{}` — future edits stay in memory only.
2. **Legacy persisted state gets wiped on load.** `onRehydrateStorage` unconditionally resets to `initialState`, forces `editMode` off, and calls `clearStorage()` — so anyone (including you) with a stale `route-edit` entry in localStorage gets cleared out on the next page load.

Reload FEMSA1 once. The stored draft will be nuked as the store rehydrates, the UI drops out of edit mode, and subsequent reloads start clean. You'll still see the applied edits (those are persisted separately via `updateLocalSolutionResult` in the local-solution store), you just won't be dropped mid-edit.

 "old_string": "/**\n * Remove a step from a route by index.\n *\n * @returns The updated route with the step removed.\n */\nexport function removeStepFromRoute(\n  route: OptimizationMvrpRoute,\n  stepIndex: number,\n): OptimizationMvrpRoute {\n  const steps = [...route.steps]\n  steps.splice(stepIndex, 1)\n  return {...route, steps}\n}",
 "new_string": "/**\n * Remove a step from a route by index.\n *\n * @returns The updated route with the step removed.\n */\nexport function removeStepFromRoute(\n  route: OptimizationMvrpRoute,\n  stepIndex: number,\n): OptimizationMvrpRoute {\n  const steps = [...route.steps]\n  steps.splice(stepIndex, 1)\n  return {...route, steps}\n}\n\n/** Parse a `\"lat,lng\"` location string → `[lng, lat]`. */\nfunction parseInputLocation(\n  input: OptimizationMvrpInputDataV2 | null,\n  index: number | undefined,\n): [number, number] | null {\n  if (input == null || index == null) return null\n  const raw = input.locations?.location?.[index]\n  if (typeof raw !== 'string') return null\n  const parts = raw.split(',')\n  if (parts.length < 2) return null\n  const lat = Number.parseFloat(parts[0])\n  const lng = Number.parseFloat(parts[1])\n  if (!Number.isFinite(lat) || !Number.isFinite(lng)) return null\n  return [lng, lat]\n}\n\n/**\n * Build a fresh route for a vehicle that was previously unassigned, seeded\n * with the given unassigned tasks in the order provided. Start/end coords\n * come from the vehicle's `start_index` / `end_index` (falling back to the\n * start when no end is set). Route-level metrics are zeroed — the caller\n * runs `applyDirectionsResult` afterwards to populate distance/duration\n * and per-step arrival times.\n */\nexport function buildRouteFromUnassignedVehicle(\n  vehicle: NonNullable<OptimizationMvrpInputDataV2['vehicles']>[number],\n  tasks: OptimizationMvrpUnassigned[],\n  input: OptimizationMvrpInputDataV2 | null,\n): OptimizationMvrpRoute | null {\n  const startLoc = parseInputLocation(input, vehicle.start_index)\n  if (!startLoc) return null\n  const endIndex =\n    vehicle.end_index != null ? vehicle.end_index : vehicle.start_index\n  const endLoc = parseInputLocation(input, endIndex) ?? startLoc\n\n  const shiftStart =\n    Array.isArray(vehicle.time_window) && vehicle.time_window.length >= 2\n      ? vehicle.time_window[0]\n      : 0\n\n  const startStep: OptimizationMvrpRouteStep = {\n    type: 'start',\n    location: startLoc,\n    location_index: vehicle.start_index,\n    arrival: shiftStart,\n    service: 0,\n    setup: 0,\n  }\n  const endStep: OptimizationMvrpRouteStep = {\n    type: 'end',\n    location: endLoc,\n    location_index: endIndex,\n    arrival: shiftStart,\n    service: 0,\n    setup: 0,\n  }\n  const taskSteps = tasks.map((t) => buildStepFromUnassigned(t, input))\n\n  return {\n    vehicle: vehicle.id,\n    description: vehicle.description,\n    cost: 0,\n    distance: 0,\n    duration: 0,\n    service: 0,\n    setup: 0,\n    waiting_time: 0,\n    revenue: 0,\n    steps: [startStep, ...taskSteps, endStep],\n    vehicle_overtime: 0,\n  }\n}"
}

Renders the input-side details\n * (description, shift window, capacity, skills, max working time, allowed\n * zones) so the user can see *why* the vehicle might have been left\n * out — the solution result drops these fields for non-routed vehicles.\n *\n * Read-only: there's no edit/drag affordance because adding a route\n * for the vehicle is a re-optimization concern, not a drag-step concern.\n */\nfunction UnassignedVehicleItem({\n  vehicle,\n  timezone,\n}: {\n  vehicle: OptimizationMvrpOrderVehicleV2\n  timezone?: string\n}) {\n  const t = useTranslations('solution')\n  const shift = vehicle.time_window\n  const capacity = vehicle.capacity\n  const skills = vehicle.skills\n  const maxWorking = vehicle.max_working_time\n  const allowedZones = vehicle.allowed_zones\n\n  return (\n    <div style={{padding: '8px 12px', margin: '0 -12px'}}>\n      <Stack direction=\"row\" alignItems=\"center\" gap={1}>\n        <Typography sx={{fontSize: 14, fontWeight: 700}}>{vehicle.id}</Typography>\n        {vehicle.description && (\n          <Typography\n            sx={{\n              fontSize: 13,\n              color: 'text.secondary',\n              overflow: 'hidden',\n              textOverflow: 'ellipsis',\n              whiteSpace: 'nowrap',\n            }}\n          >\n            {vehicle.description}\n          </Typography>\n        )}\n      </Stack>",
 "new_string": "// ── UnassignedVehicleItem ─────────────────────────────────\n\n/**\n * Card for a vehicle that was in the original input but didn't end up\n * with a route in the solution. Renders the input-side details\n * (description, shift window, capacity, skills, max working time, allowed\n * zones) so the user can see *why* the vehicle might have been left\n * out — the solution result drops these fields for non-routed vehicles.\n *\n * In edit mode: exposes an \"Assign tasks\" action that opens a picker of\n * currently-unassigned tasks; picking one or more spins up a fresh route\n * for this vehicle (see `assignUnassignedTasksToVehicle` in the edit store).\n */\nfunction UnassignedVehicleItem({\n  vehicle,\n  editMode,\n  timezone,\n}: {\n  vehicle: OptimizationMvrpOrderVehicleV2\n  editMode?: boolean\n  timezone?: string\n}) {\n  const t = useTranslations('solution')\n  const shift = vehicle.time_window\n  const capacity = vehicle.capacity\n  const skills = vehicle.skills\n  const maxWorking = vehicle.max_working_time\n  const allowedZones = vehicle.allowed_zones\n\n  const draftUnassigned = useRouteEditStore((s) => s.draft?.unassigned)\n  const assignUnassignedTasksToVehicle = useRouteEditStore(\n    (s) => s.assignUnassignedTasksToVehicle,\n  )\n\n  const [pickerAnchor, setPickerAnchor] = useState<HTMLElement | null>(null)\n  const [pickedTaskUids, setPickedTaskUids] = useState<Set<string>>(new Set())\n  const [taskFilter, setTaskFilter] = useState('')\n  const [assigning, setAssigning] = useState(false)\n\n  const pickerTasks = useMemo(() => {\n    if (!draftUnassigned) return []\n    const q = taskFilter.trim().toLowerCase()\n    return draftUnassigned\n      .map((task, idx) => ({\n        task,\n        // Uid = id + type so pickup/delivery pairs stay distinguishable.\n        uid: `${task.id}-${task.type ?? task.task_type ?? 'job'}-${idx}`,\n      }))\n      .filter(({task}) => {\n        if (!q) return true\n        if (String(task.id).toLowerCase().includes(q)) return true\n        return task.description?.toLowerCase().includes(q) ?? false\n      })\n  }, [draftUnassigned, taskFilter])\n\n  const openPicker = useCallback((el: HTMLElement) => {\n    setPickerAnchor(el)\n    setPickedTaskUids(new Set())\n    setTaskFilter('')\n  }, [])\n\n  const closePicker = useCallback(() => {\n    setPickerAnchor(null)\n  }, [])\n\n  const togglePicked = useCallback((uid: string) => {\n    setPickedTaskUids((prev) => {\n      const next = new Set(prev)\n      if (next.has(uid)) next.delete(uid)\n      else next.add(uid)\n      return next\n    })\n  }, [])\n\n  const handleAssign = useCallback(async () => {\n    const selected = pickerTasks\n      .filter((row) => pickedTaskUids.has(row.uid))\n      .map((row) => ({\n        id: row.task.id,\n        type: row.task.type ?? row.task.task_type ?? 'job',\n      }))\n    if (selected.length === 0) return\n    setAssigning(true)\n    try {\n      await assignUnassignedTasksToVehicle(String(vehicle.id), selected)\n      notify(t('assignTasksSuccess', {count: selected.length}), {severity: 'success'})\n      closePicker()\n    } catch (error) {\n      notify(\n        error instanceof Error ? error.message : t('assignTasksError'),\n        {severity: 'error'},\n      )\n    } finally {\n      setAssigning(false)\n    }\n  }, [pickerTasks, pickedTaskUids, assignUnassignedTasksToVehicle, vehicle.id, closePicker, t])\n\n  return (\n    <div style={{padding: '8px 12px', margin: '0 -12px'}}>\n      <Stack direction=\"row\" alignItems=\"center\" justifyContent=\"space-between\" gap={1}>\n        <Stack direction=\"row\" alignItems=\"center\" gap={1} sx={{minWidth: 0, flex: 1}}>\n          <Typography sx={{fontSize: 14, fontWeight: 700}}>{vehicle.id}</Typography>\n          {vehicle.description && (\n            <Typography\n              sx={{\n                fontSize: 13,\n                color: 'text.secondary',\n                overflow: 'hidden',\n                textOverflow: 'ellipsis',\n                whiteSpace: 'nowrap',\n              }}\n            >\n              {vehicle.description}\n            </Typography>\n          )}\n        </Stack>\n        {editMode && (draftUnassigned?.length ?? 0) > 0 && (\n          <Button\n            size=\"small\"\n            variant=\"outlined\"\n            onClick={(e) => openPicker(e.currentTarget)}\n            sx={{\n              textTransform: 'none',\n              fontSize: 12,\n              fontWeight: 600,\n              px: 1.25,\n              py: 0.25,\n              minHeight: 26,\n              borderRadius: '8px',\n            }}\n          >\n            {t('assignTasksButton')}\n          </Button>\n        )}\n      </Stack>"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-07-13T15:28:13.908Z)

Done. New capability, wired end-to-end:

**Store (`route-edit.store.ts`)**
- New action `assignUnassignedTasksToVehicle(vehicleId, tasks)`:
  - Refuses if the vehicle already has a draft route.
  - Looks up the vehicle in `input.vehicles`, resolves start/end coords via `input.locations.location[start_index | end_index]`.
  - Builds a fresh route (`start` → task steps in the picked order → `end`), removes the tasks from `draft.unassigned`.
  - Calls Directions for that route and runs `applyDirectionsResult` to fill distances/durations/arrivals.
  - Wraps everything in the same snapshot/undo/error-rollback pattern as `moveUnassignedToRoute`.

**Domain helper (`step-operations.ts`)**
- New `buildRouteFromUnassignedVehicle(vehicle, tasks, input)` — pure route-skeleton builder, returns `null` when no start location resolves.
- New `parseInputLocation` — internal helper for the "lat,lng" → `[lng, lat]` conversion.

**UI (`result-panel.tsx`, `UnassignedVehicleItem`)**
- In edit mode with at least one unassigned task, the card shows an **Assign tasks** button on the right.
- Click opens a Popover picker with a search box + checkbox list of `draft.unassigned` (id, description, type).
- **Assign** button fires the store action, notifies success/error, closes the popover.
- Disabled while the request is in flight ("Assigning…").

**i18n**
- `assignTasksButton / Title / SearchPlaceholder / Empty / Cancel / Confirm / Assigning / Success / Error` in en, pt-BR, es-MX, fr-CA, pl-PL.

Enter edit mode, jump to the **Unassigned Vehicles** tab, pick a vehicle, hit **Assign tasks**, tick some unassigned tasks, hit **Assign** — you should see a new route appear in the Routes tab with its own polyline once Directions comes back.

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:
1. Call CronCreate with: `cron` (the expression above), `prompt` (the parsed prompt verbatim), `recurring: true`.
2. Briefly confirm: what's scheduled, the cron expression, the human-readable cadence, that recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days, and that the user can cancel sooner with CronDelete (include the job ID). Only if you did NOT show the cloud-offer AskUserQuestion above (i.e., neither trigger condition applied), end the confirmation with this exact line on its own, italicized: `_Runs until you close this session · For durable cloud-based loops, use /schedule_`. If the user already answered that question, omit this line.
3. **Then immediately execute the parsed prompt now** — don't wait for the first cron fire. If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.

## Dynamic mode (rule 3 — no interval)

The user wants you to self-pace. Decide what makes the next iteration worth running — a passage of time, or an observable event.

1. **Run the parsed prompt now.** If it's a slash command, invoke it via the Skill tool; otherwise act on it directly.
2. **If the next run is gated on an event** (CI finishing, a log line matching, a file changing, a PR comment) and no Monitor is already running for it: arm one now with `persistent: true`. Its events arrive as `<task-notification>` messages and wake this loop immediately — you do not wait for the ScheduleWakeup deadline. Arm once; on later iterations call TaskList first and skip this step if a monitor is already running.
3. **Briefly confirm**: that you're self-pacing, whether a Monitor is the primary wake signal, that you ran the task now, and what fallback delay you're about to pick. Write this as text *before* calling ScheduleWakeup — the turn ends as soon as that tool returns.
4. **Then, as the last action of this turn, decide whether the loop continues.** If the task needs another iteration, call ScheduleWakeup with:
   - `delaySeconds`: with a Monitor armed this is the **fallback heartbeat** — how long to wait if no event fires (lean 1200–1800s; idle ticks more frequent than the task needs are pure overhead). Without a Monitor this is the cadence — pick based on what you observed. Read the tool's own description for cache-aware delay guidance.
   - `reason`: one short sentence on why you picked that delay.
   - `prompt`: the full original /loop input verbatim, prefixed with `/loop ` so the next firing re-enters this skill and continues the loop. For example, if the user typed `/loop check the deploy`, pass `/loop check the deploy` as the prompt.
   If it doesn't need another iteration, stop instead (step 6) — re-arming is a per-turn choice, not a default.
5. **If you were woken by a `<task-notification>`** rather than this prompt: handle the event in the context of the loop task, then make the same decision. If the loop should continue, call ScheduleWakeup again with the same `prompt` and the same 1200–1800s `delaySeconds` from step 4 (the Monitor remains the wake signal; the new wakeup is only the fallback heartbeat). If the event means the work is finished, stop (step 6).
6. **To stop the loop** — the task is complete, further iterations can't make progress, or the user asked you to stop — call ScheduleWakeup with `stop: true` (no other fields) and TaskStop any Monitor you armed (use TaskList to find the task ID if it is no longer in context). Stopping is the loop's normal ending — the user can restart it anytime with /loop.

[]\n    const inputVehicle = rawInputVehicles?.find(\n      (v) => String(v.id) === selectedVehicleId,\n    )\n    const hasStart =\n      inputVehicle == null ||\n      (inputVehicle.start_index !== undefined &&\n        inputVehicle.start_index !== null)\n    const hasEnd =\n      inputVehicle == null ||\n      (inputVehicle.end_index !== undefined &&\n        inputVehicle.end_index !== null)\n\n    // Reproduce skipLeadingRest's drop rules while tracking raw indices.\n    const isRest = (t?: string) => t === 'break' || t === 'layover'\n    const skipFirst = src.length > 0 && isRest(src[0]?.type)\n    const skipSecond =\n      !skipFirst &&\n      src.length > 1 &&\n      src[0]?.type === 'start' &&\n      isRest(src[1]?.type)\n\n    const visible: typeof src = []\n    const indices: number[] = []\n    src.forEach((step, i) => {\n      if (skipFirst && i === 0) return\n      if (skipSecond && i === 1) return\n      if (step.type === 'start' && !hasStart) return\n      if (step.type === 'end' && !hasEnd) return\n      visible.push(step)\n      indices.push(i)\n    })\n    return {steps: visible, rawStepIndexOf: indices}\n  }, [route, rawInputVehicles, selectedVehicleId])",
 "new_string": "  // Drop a leading break/layover so the manifest's \"first stop\" is\n  // always the real start step. Mirrored in use-map-layers.ts so the\n  // map and the manifest agree on which steps exist.\n  //\n  // Also hide synthetic start/end pseudo-steps when the input vehicle\n  // never declared a corresponding depot index — matches the map's\n  // suppression of S/E markers for those vehicles.\n  //\n  // trimmedStepIndexOf[i] is the position of the visible step in the\n  // POST-skipLeadingRest step array (which is what use-map-layers.ts\n  // uses as its hover-key `stepOrder`). Passing the filtered position\n  // instead would offset hover highlighting by the number of hidden\n  // start/end pseudo-steps preceding the row.\n  const {steps, trimmedStepIndexOf} = useMemo(() => {\n    const trimmed = skipLeadingRest(route?.steps ?? [])\n    const inputVehicle = rawInputVehicles?.find(\n      (v) => String(v.id) === selectedVehicleId,\n    )\n    const hasStart =\n      inputVehicle == null ||\n      (inputVehicle.start_index !== undefined &&\n        inputVehicle.start_index !== null)\n    const hasEnd =\n      inputVehicle == null ||\n      (inputVehicle.end_index !== undefined &&\n        inputVehicle.end_index !== null)\n\n    const visible: typeof trimmed = []\n    const indices: number[] = []\n    trimmed.forEach((step, i) => {\n      if (step.type === 'start' && !hasStart) return\n      if (step.type === 'end' && !hasEnd) return\n      visible.push(step)\n      indices.push(i)\n    })\n    return {steps: visible, trimmedStepIndexOf: indices}\n  }, [route, rawInputVehicles, selectedVehicleId])"
}

 "old_string": "type ZoneFilterOption = {id: string; label: string}\n\nfunction RouteZoneFilter() {\n  const t = useTranslations('solution')\n  const zones = useSolutionStore((s) => s._rawInput?.zones)\n  const selectedZoneIds = useUIStore((s) => s.selectedZoneIds)\n  const setSelectedZoneIds = useUIStore((s) => s.setSelectedZoneIds)\n\n  const options: ZoneFilterOption[] = useMemo(() => {\n    if (!zones?.length) return []\n    return zones\n      .filter((z) => z.geometry)\n      .map((z) => ({\n        id: String(z.id),\n        label: z.name?.trim() ? z.name : `Zone ${z.id}`,\n      }))\n      .sort((a, b) => {\n        const na = Number(a.id)\n        const nb = Number(b.id)\n        if (Number.isFinite(na) && Number.isFinite(nb)) return na - nb\n        return a.id.localeCompare(b.id)\n      })\n  }, [zones])\n\n  const value = useMemo(\n    () => options.filter((o) => selectedZoneIds.includes(o.id)),\n    [options, selectedZoneIds],\n  )\n\n  return (\n    <Autocomplete<ZoneFilterOption, true>\n      multiple\n      size=\"small\"\n      options={options}\n      value={value}\n      onChange={(_e, next) => setSelectedZoneIds(next.map((o) => o.id))}\n      getOptionLabel={(opt) => opt.label}\n      isOptionEqualToValue={(a, b) => a.id === b.id}\n      noOptionsText={t('zoneFilterEmpty')}\n      renderTags={(tags, getTagProps) =>\n        tags.map((opt, i) => (\n          <Chip\n            size=\"small\"\n            label={opt.label}\n            {...getTagProps({index: i})}\n            key={opt.id}\n          />\n        ))\n      }\n      renderInput={(params) => (\n        <TextField\n          {...params}\n          label={t('zoneFilterLabel')}\n          placeholder={\n            value.length === 0 ? t('zoneFilterPlaceholder') : undefined\n          }\n          size=\"small\"\n        />\n      )}\n      sx={{'& .MuiInputBase-input': {fontSize: 13}}}\n    />\n  )\n}",
 "new_string": "// Day-aggregated option. `day` is the day-of-week integer (Sunday=1..\n// Saturday=7) parsed from FEMSA-style zone names via\n// parseZoneDayOfWeek. `zoneIds` is every input-zone id whose name\n// resolves to that day — selecting the option toggles all of them at\n// once so the user doesn't have to hunt through the per-zone list.\ntype ZoneFilterOption = {day: number; label: string; zoneIds: string[]}\n\nfunction RouteZoneFilter() {\n  const t = useTranslations('solution')\n  const zones = useSolutionStore((s) => s._rawInput?.zones)\n  const selectedZoneIds = useUIStore((s) => s.selectedZoneIds)\n  const setSelectedZoneIds = useUIStore((s) => s.setSelectedZoneIds)\n\n  const options: ZoneFilterOption[] = useMemo(() => {\n    if (!zones?.length) return []\n    const byDay = new Map<number, string[]>()\n    for (const z of zones) {\n      if (!z.geometry) continue\n      const day = parseZoneDayOfWeek(z.name)\n      if (day == null) continue\n      const list = byDay.get(day) ?? []\n      list.push(String(z.id))\n      byDay.set(day, list)\n    }\n    return [...byDay.entries()]\n      .sort((a, b) => a[0] - b[0])\n      .map(([day, zoneIds]) => ({\n        day,\n        label: `Zone-${day}`,\n        zoneIds,\n      }))\n  }, [zones])\n\n  const selectedSet = useMemo(\n    () => new Set(selectedZoneIds),\n    [selectedZoneIds],\n  )\n\n  // A day is \"selected\" when every zone belonging to that day is in the\n  // stored id set. Partial selections (from a prior fine-grained filter\n  // shape) don't light up the chip but also don't blow away the state.\n  const value = useMemo(\n    () =>\n      options.filter(\n        (o) =>\n          o.zoneIds.length > 0 && o.zoneIds.every((id) => selectedSet.has(id)),\n      ),\n    [options, selectedSet],\n  )\n\n  return (\n    <Autocomplete<ZoneFilterOption, true>\n      multiple\n      size=\"small\"\n      options={options}\n      value={value}\n      onChange={(_e, next) => {\n        const nextDays = new Set(next.map((o) => o.day))\n        // Rebuild the id set from scratch: keep anything the day\n        // aggregator can't classify (unmatched zone names remain\n        // untouched by this filter) plus every id for the newly\n        // selected days.\n        const managedIds = new Set(options.flatMap((o) => o.zoneIds))\n        const kept = selectedZoneIds.filter((id) => !managedIds.has(id))\n        const added = next.flatMap((o) =>\n          nextDays.has(o.day) ? o.zoneIds : [],\n        )\n        setSelectedZoneIds([...new Set([...kept, ...added])])\n      }}\n      getOptionLabel={(opt) => opt.label}\n      isOptionEqualToValue={(a, b) => a.day === b.day}\n      noOptionsText={t('zoneFilterEmpty')}\n      renderTags={(tags, getTagProps) =>\n        tags.map((opt, i) => (\n          <Chip\n            size=\"small\"\n            label={opt.label}\n            {...getTagProps({index: i})}\n            key={opt.day}\n          />\n        ))\n      }\n      renderInput={(params) => (\n        <TextField\n          {...params}\n          label={t('zoneFilterLabel')}\n          placeholder={\n            value.length === 0 ? t('zoneFilterPlaceholder') : undefined\n          }\n          size=\"small\"\n        />\n      )}\n      sx={{'& .MuiInputBase-input': {fontSize: 13}}}\n    />\n  )\n}"
}

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/libs/territory-planner/src/run.js",
 "content": "'use strict';\n\nconst {parseBase} = require('./parse');\nconst {buildTerritories} = require('./cluster');\nconst {scheduleAll} = require('./schedule');\nconst {validate} = require('./validate');\nconst {buildBoundaries} = require('./boundaries');\n\n/**\n * End-to-end pipeline. Mirrors cli.js stages 1-5 but returns the results\n * as a JS object instead of writing files. Stage 6 (workbook / summary\n * disk output) is intentionally omitted — the API route can call\n * buildWorkbook / buildSummary itself if it wants those artifacts.\n *\n * @param {string|Buffer|ArrayBuffer} input   xlsx file path OR upload buffer\n * @param {(msg: string) => void} [onLog]     progress callback per stage\n * @returns {Promise<{\n *   pos: Array<object>,\n *   R: number,\n *   proj: {lat0: number, lon0: number, kx: number, ky: number},\n *   boundaries: {type: 'FeatureCollection', features: Array<object>},\n *   slotLoads: number[][][],\n *   metrics: object,\n *   excluded: number,\n * }>}\n */\nasync function runPipeline(input, onLog) {\n  const log = onLog || (() => {});\n\n  log('[1/5] Parsing input workbook...');\n  const {pos, excluded, proj} = await parseBase(input);\n  log(\n    `  ${pos.length} active POS (${excluded} zero-frequency excluded), ` +\n      `${pos.reduce((a, p) => a + p.freq * 4, 0)} visits over 4 weeks`,\n  );\n\n  log('[2/5] Building balanced territories (transportation LP)...');\n  const {R} = await buildTerritories(pos, log);\n  log(`  ${R} territories`);\n\n  log('[3/5] Scheduling visit days/weeks (per-territory MILP)...');\n  const slotLoads = await scheduleAll(pos, R, log);\n\n  log('[4/5] Validating solution...');\n  const {ok, errors, metrics} = validate(pos, R, slotLoads);\n  if (!ok) {\n    const preview = errors.slice(0, 20).join('\\n  ');\n    throw new Error(`Validation failed:\\n  ${preview}`);\n  }\n  log(\n    `  OK — max rep-day ${metrics.maxSlotH} h ` +\n      `(cap ${metrics.dailyCapH} h), 0 violations`,\n  );\n\n  log('[5/5] Building territory boundaries...');\n  const boundaries = buildBoundaries(pos, R, proj);\n  log(`  ${boundaries.features.length} territory polygons`);\n\n  return {pos, R, proj, boundaries, slotLoads, metrics, excluded};\n}\n\nmodule.exports = {runPipeline};\n"
}
```

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/apps/route-planner-v2/app/api/territory-planner/route.ts",
 "content": "// Territory planner pipeline endpoint.\n//\n// POST a multipart/form-data body with a `file` field containing the FEMSA\n// base workbook (.xlsx). The handler streams NDJSON events over the response\n// body:\n//   { type: 'log',    message: string }              — progress lines\n//   { type: 'result', result: TerritoryPipelineResult } — final payload\n//   { type: 'error',  message: string }              — pipeline failure\n//\n// NDJSON (not SSE) keeps parsing trivial on the client side — one JSON\n// object per line — while still allowing the ~2-min pipeline to report\n// interim progress. The final `result` event carries every field the\n// map page needs (pos, R, boundaries, metrics), so the client doesn't\n// need a second round-trip.\n\nimport {runPipeline} from '@ncc/territory-planner'\n\n// Long-running (~2 min on 6.5k POS). Keep on the Node runtime with a\n// generous timeout so Cloud Run / Vercel don't cut the response.\nexport const runtime = 'nodejs'\nexport const maxDuration = 300\n\nexport async function POST(request: Request) {\n  let file: File | null = null\n  try {\n    const form = await request.formData()\n    const raw = form.get('file')\n    if (raw instanceof File) file = raw\n  } catch {\n    return Response.json({error: 'invalid multipart body'}, {status: 400})\n  }\n  if (!file) {\n    return Response.json(\n      {error: 'missing \"file\" field (upload the base .xlsx)'},\n      {status: 400},\n    )\n  }\n  const buf = Buffer.from(await file.arrayBuffer())\n\n  const stream = new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({\n    async start(controller) {\n      const enc = new TextEncoder()\n      const send = (obj: unknown) =>\n        controller.enqueue(enc.encode(JSON.stringify(obj) + '\\n'))\n      try {\n        const result = await runPipeline(buf, (message) =>\n          send({type: 'log', message}),\n        )\n        send({type: 'result', result: serializeResult(result)})\n      } catch (err) {\n        const message = err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err)\n        send({type: 'error', message})\n      } finally {\n        controller.close()\n      }\n    },\n  })\n\n  return new Response(stream, {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: {\n      'Content-Type': 'application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8',\n      'Cache-Control': 'no-store, no-transform',\n      // Disable proxy buffering so progress lines actually flush.\n      'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no',\n    },\n  })\n}\n\n// The internal POS records carry Set<number> fields (`avail`, `restr`,\n// `eff`) that don't survive JSON.stringify. Drop them and everything\n// else the client doesn't render — the map only needs identity, coords,\n// schedule, territory, and workload.\nfunction serializeResult(r: Awaited<ReturnType<typeof runPipeline>>) {\n  return {\n    R: r.R,\n    excluded: r.excluded,\n    metrics: r.metrics,\n    boundaries: r.boundaries,\n    pos: r.pos.map((p) => ({\n      matricula: p.matricula,\n      lat: p.lat,\n      lon: p.lon,\n      terr: p.terr,\n      freq: p.freq,\n      tempoH: Number(p.tempoH.toFixed(3)),\n      visitH: Number(p.visitH.toFixed(3)),\n      weekH: Number(p.weekH.toFixed(3)),\n      schedDays: p.schedDays,\n      schedWeeks: p.schedWeeks,\n      tipo: p.tipo,\n    })),\n  }\n}\n"
}

 "content": "'use client'\n\nimport {useContext, useEffect, useMemo, useState} from 'react'\nimport {AppContext} from '@ncc/common/client'\nimport type {Layer} from '@deck.gl/core/typed'\nimport {GeoJsonLayer, ScatterplotLayer} from '@deck.gl/layers/typed'\nimport type {ViewState} from 'react-map-gl'\nimport {BaseMap} from '../../v3/components/map/base-map'\nimport {useMapStyle} from '../../utils/map-style'\nimport type {TerritoryResult, TerritoryPos} from './types'\n\n// Distinct, ~evenly spaced hues around the color wheel so adjacent\n// territories don't collide. HSL → RGB stays cheap and produces a\n// consistent palette regardless of R.\nfunction territoryColor(t: number, R: number): [number, number, number] {\n  const hue = (t * 360) / Math.max(R, 1)\n  return hslToRgb(hue, 65, 50)\n}\n\nfunction hslToRgb(h: number, s: number, l: number): [number, number, number] {\n  const sN = s / 100\n  const lN = l / 100\n  const c = (1 - Math.abs(2 * lN - 1)) * sN\n  const hp = h / 60\n  const x = c * (1 - Math.abs((hp % 2) - 1))\n  let r = 0\n  let g = 0\n  let b = 0\n  if (hp < 1) [r, g, b] = [c, x, 0]\n  else if (hp < 2) [r, g, b] = [x, c, 0]\n  else if (hp < 3) [r, g, b] = [0, c, x]\n  else if (hp < 4) [r, g, b] = [0, x, c]\n  else if (hp < 5) [r, g, b] = [x, 0, c]\n  else [r, g, b] = [c, 0, x]\n  const m = lN - c / 2\n  return [\n    Math.round((r + m) * 255),\n    Math.round((g + m) * 255),\n    Math.round((b + m) * 255),\n  ]\n}\n\n// Fit `viewState` to a bounding box of all POS. Cheap replacement for\n// react-map-gl's fitBounds — good enough for an initial framing.\nfunction boundsToViewState(\n  pos: TerritoryPos[],\n  width: number,\n  height: number,\n): Partial<ViewState> {\n  if (!pos.length) return {longitude: 0, latitude: 0, zoom: 2}\n  let minLon = Infinity\n  let maxLon = -Infinity\n  let minLat = Infinity\n  let maxLat = -Infinity\n  for (const p of pos) {\n    if (p.lon < minLon) minLon = p.lon\n    if (p.lon > maxLon) maxLon = p.lon\n    if (p.lat < minLat) minLat = p.lat\n    if (p.lat > maxLat) maxLat = p.lat\n  }\n  const lonSpan = Math.max(maxLon - minLon, 0.0001)\n  const latSpan = Math.max(maxLat - minLat, 0.0001)\n  // Web-mercator rough zoom fit — enough to center everything with padding.\n  const zoomLon = Math.log2((width * 360) / (lonSpan * 512))\n  const zoomLat = Math.log2((height * 360) / (latSpan * 512))\n  return {\n    longitude: (minLon + maxLon) / 2,\n    latitude: (minLat + maxLat) / 2,\n    zoom: Math.max(2, Math.min(zoomLon, zoomLat) - 0.5),\n    pitch: 0,\n    bearing: 0,\n  }\n}\n\nexport function TerritoryMap({result}: {result: TerritoryResult}) {\n  const [{currentApiKey}] = useContext(AppContext)\n  const mapStyle = useMapStyle(currentApiKey?.kid)\n  const [viewState, setViewState] = useState<Partial<ViewState>>({\n    longitude: 0,\n    latitude: 0,\n    zoom: 2,\n  })\n  const [hover, setHover] = useState<{\n    terr: number\n    x: number\n    y: number\n  } | null>(null)\n\n  useEffect(() => {\n    // Frame all POS on first mount / when a new result comes in.\n    // Approximate the viewport size — the container fills the panel.\n    const w =\n      typeof window !== 'undefined' ? window.innerWidth * 0.7 : 900\n    const h = typeof window !== 'undefined' ? window.innerHeight * 0.8 : 700\n    setViewState((vs) => ({...vs, ...boundsToViewState(result.pos, w, h)}))\n  }, [result])\n\n  const layers: Layer[] = useMemo(() => {\n    // Boundary polygons — fill semi-transparent per territory, matching\n    // the point color so the same-territory relationship is obvious at\n    // a glance.\n    const boundary = new GeoJsonLayer({\n      id: 'territory-boundaries',\n      data: result.boundaries,\n      stroked: true,\n      filled: true,\n      pickable: true,\n      lineWidthMinPixels: 1.5,\n      getFillColor: (f: {properties?: {terr?: number}}) => {\n        const [r, g, b] = territoryColor(\n          f.properties?.terr ?? 0,\n          result.R,\n        )\n        return [r, g, b, 50]\n      },\n      getLineColor: (f: {properties?: {terr?: number}}) => {\n        const [r, g, b] = territoryColor(\n          f.properties?.terr ?? 0,\n          result.R,\n        )\n        return [r, g, b, 220]\n      },\n      onHover: (info) => {\n        if (info.object) {\n          setHover({\n            terr: (info.object.properties as {terr: number}).terr,\n            x: info.x,\n            y: info.y,\n          })\n        } else {\n          setHover(null)\n        }\n      },\n    })\n    // POS points, colored by territory. Radius scales gently with\n    // visit frequency so freq-2 sites stand out.\n    const points = new ScatterplotLayer<TerritoryPos>({\n      id: 'territory-pos',\n      data: result.pos,\n      getPosition: (p) => [p.lon, p.lat],\n      getRadius: (p) => 3 + p.freq * 1.5,\n      radiusUnits: 'pixels',\n      getFillColor: (p) => {\n        const [r, g, b] = territoryColor(p.terr, result.R)\n        return [r, g, b, 220]\n      },\n      stroked: true,\n      lineWidthMinPixels: 0.5,\n      getLineColor: [255, 255, 255, 220],\n      pickable: false,\n    })\n    return [boundary, points]\n  }, [result])\n\n  if (!mapStyle) {\n    return (\n      <div\n        style={{\n          display: 'flex',\n          alignItems: 'center',\n          justifyContent: 'center',\n          height: '100%',\n          color: '#626B84',\n          fontSize: 14,\n        }}\n      >\n        Loading map…\n      </div>\n    )\n  }\n\n  const territoryStats = useMemo(() => {\n    const stats = new Map<\n      number,\n      {count: number; weekH: number}\n    >()\n    for (const p of result.pos) {\n      const s = stats.get(p.terr) ?? {count: 0, weekH: 0}\n      s.count += 1\n      s.weekH += p.weekH\n      stats.set(p.terr, s)\n    }\n    return stats\n  }, [result.pos])\n\n  return (\n    <div\n      style={{\n        position: 'relative',\n        width: '100%',\n        height: '100%',\n      }}\n    >\n      <BaseMap\n        layers={layers}\n        viewState={viewState}\n        onViewStateChange={setViewState}\n        mapStyle={mapStyle as unknown as string}\n        mapId=\"territoryPlannerMap\"\n      >\n        <></>\n      </BaseMap>\n      {hover && (\n        <div\n          style={{\n            position: 'absolute',\n            left: hover.x + 12,\n            top: hover.y + 12,\n            padding: '6px 10px',\n            background: 'rgba(20, 24, 40, 0.92)',\n            color: '#fff',\n            borderRadius: 6,\n            fontSize: 12,\n            pointerEvents: 'none',\n            zIndex: 10,\n            whiteSpace: 'nowrap',\n          }}\n        >\n          Territory {hover.terr + 1}\n          {territoryStats.get(hover.terr) && (\n            <>\n              {' · '}\n              {territoryStats.get(hover.terr)?.count} POS ·{' '}\n              {territoryStats.get(hover.terr)?.weekH.toFixed(0)} h/wk\n            </>\n          )}\n        </div>\n      )}\n    </div>\n  )\n}\n"

# /loop — schedule a recurring or self-paced prompt

Parse the input below into `[interval] <prompt…>` and schedule it.

## Parsing (in priority order)

1. **Leading token**: if the first whitespace-delimited token matches `^\d+[smhd]$` (e.g. `5m`, `2h`), that's the interval; the rest is the prompt.
2. **Trailing "every" clause**: otherwise, if the input ends with `every <N><unit>` or `every <N> <unit-word>` (e.g. `every 20m`, `every 5 minutes`, `every 2 hours`), extract that as the interval and strip it from the prompt. Only match when what follows "every" is a time expression — `check every PR` has no interval.
3. **No interval**: otherwise, the entire input is the prompt and you'll self-pace dynamically (see "Dynamic mode" below).

If the resulting prompt is empty, show usage `/loop [interval] <prompt>` and stop.

Examples:
- `5m /babysit-prs` → interval `5m`, prompt `/babysit-prs` (rule 1)
- `check the deploy every 20m` → interval `20m`, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 2)
- `run tests every 5 minutes` → interval `5m`, prompt `run tests` (rule 2)
- `check the deploy` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check the deploy` (rule 3)
- `check every PR` → no interval → dynamic mode, prompt `check every PR` (rule 3 — "every" not followed by time)
- `5m` → empty prompt → show usage

## Offer cloud first

Before any scheduling step, check whether EITHER is true:
- the parsed interval (rule 1 or 2) is **≥60 minutes**, or
- regardless of which rule matched, the original input uses daily phrasing ("every morning", "daily", "every day", "each night", "every weekday")

If either is true, call AskUserQuestion first:
- `question`: "This loop stops when you close this session. Set it up as a cloud schedule instead so it keeps running?"
- `header`: "Schedule"
- `options`: `[{label: "Cloud schedule (recommended)", description: "Runs in Anthropic's cloud even after you close this session"}, {label: "This session only", description: "Runs in this terminal until you exit"}]`

If they pick **Cloud schedule**: do NOT call CronCreate. Invoke the `schedule` skill directly via the Skill tool with `args` set to their original input verbatim (e.g. `Skill({skill: "schedule", args: "every morning tell me a joke"})`), then follow that skill's instructions to completion. Do NOT tell the user to run /schedule themselves. **Then stop — do not continue to any section below** (no CronCreate, no ScheduleWakeup, no "execute the prompt now").
If they pick **This session only**:
- If the trigger was a parsed ≥60-minute interval (rule 1 or 2): continue below with that interval.
- If the trigger was daily phrasing only (rule 3, no parsed interval): do NOT call CronCreate. Explain that a daily-cadence loop won't fire before this session closes, so there's nothing useful to schedule locally — suggest they either pick Cloud schedule, or re-run `/loop` with an explicit shorter interval (e.g. `/loop 1h <prompt>`) if they want a session loop. Then stop.
If neither trigger condition was met: continue below.

## Fixed-interval mode (rules 1 and 2)

Convert the interval to a cron expression:

| Interval pattern      | Cron expression     | Notes                                    |
|-----------------------|---------------------|------------------------------------------|
| `Nm` where N ≤ 59   | `*/N * * * *`     | every N minutes                          |
| `Nm` where N ≥ 60   | `0 */H * * *`     | round to hours (H = N/60, must divide 24)|
| `Nh` where N ≤ 23   | `0 */N * * *`     | every N hours                            |
| `Nd`                | `0 0 */N * *`     | every N days at midnight local           |
| `Ns`                | treat as `ceil(N/60)m` | cron minimum granularity is 1 minute  |

**If the interval doesn't cleanly divide its unit** (e.g. `7m` → `*/7 * * * *` gives uneven gaps at :56→:00; `90m` → 1.5h which cron can't express), pick the nearest clean interval and tell the user what you rounded to before scheduling.

Then:

### USER (2026-07-22T18:08:49.987Z)

for distance calculation in the territory planning pipeline, can we switch from haversine distance to using nextbillion.ai directions or distance matrix service for the calculation?


### CLAUDE (2026-07-22T18:09:40.314Z)

Most of the pipeline's distance use is *structural* (Voronoi boundaries, capacitated k-means centroids, LP cell-to-centroid objective, MILP spatial affinity) — those need Euclidean geometry to work at all, so a full swap would require redesigning as k-medoids over a precomputed 6.5k×6.5k NB matrix, which is a much bigger project.

The one place a real road-distance call gives clean value is `geo.js::travelPerVisitH()` — the BHH estimator that feeds rep-count sizing via the fixed `CIRCUITY = 1.4` multiplier. The pragmatic swap: keep the Euclidean geometry, but per territory (once per outer iteration) sample a handful of POS pairs through NB Distance Matrix and use the empirical straight-line-to-network ratio as that territory's circuity, or even directly compute the BHH travel estimate from the actual measured pair-distances. That's ~R territory-scoped matrix calls per iteration (~4 iterations × R ≤ 50 = a couple hundred calls total on the 6.5k dataset), not 42M pair calls.

Which do you want:
1. Just calibrate a single global `CIRCUITY` from a sample once at pipeline start (cheapest, small accuracy win).
2. Per-territory circuity from sampled pairs each iteration (recommended — matches urban-density variation, still cheap).
3. Full swap to precomputed NxN matrix + k-medoids algorithm (biggest lift, biggest change to results).


### USER (2026-07-22T18:10:32.061Z)

2

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/libs/territory-planner/src/matrix.js",
 "content": "'use strict';\n\n/**\n * NextBillion.ai Distance Matrix client, scoped to what the territory\n * pipeline needs: measure empirical road-circuity per territory by\n * comparing straight-line distances (in the pipeline's local km projection)\n * against network distances returned by /distancematrix/json.\n *\n * We deliberately keep this stateless and side-effect free: buildTerritories\n * chooses when to call it, this file just executes the API request and\n * returns numbers.\n */\n\nconst NB_BASE_URL = 'https://api.nextbillion.io';\nconst DM_PATH = '/distancematrix/json';\n\n// Sample size per territory. 8 POS → 8×8 = 64 cells (56 non-diagonal),\n// well under the DM lite cap (100×100), enough data for a robust mean\n// ratio, and keeps the total request budget small even for 50 territories.\nconst SAMPLE_PER_TERR = 8;\n\n// Minimum straight-line separation (km) between two sampled points for\n// the pair to count in the ratio. Very short pairs blow up the ratio\n// (a 30 m straight line and 90 m road is 3× circuity but not meaningful).\nconst MIN_PAIR_KM = 0.5;\n\n/** Deterministic uniform sample. Seed derived from the point count so\n *  the same territory samples the same way across pipeline reruns. */\nfunction samplePos(pts, k) {\n  if (pts.length <= k) return pts.slice();\n  let s = pts.length * 2654435761;\n  const rnd = () => {\n    s = (s * 1103515245 + 12345) & 0x7fffffff;\n    return s / 0x7fffffff;\n  };\n  const picked = new Set();\n  while (picked.size < k) picked.add(Math.floor(rnd() * pts.length));\n  return [...picked].map((i) => pts[i]);\n}\n\n/** Empirical circuity for one territory: mean (network km / straight km)\n *  over sampled point pairs. Returns null if the sample was too small\n *  or every pair got rejected. */\nasync function measureTerritoryCircuity(pts, apiKey, log) {\n  if (!apiKey || pts.length < 3) return null;\n\n  const sample = samplePos(pts, SAMPLE_PER_TERR);\n  const coordStr = sample.map((p) => `${p.lat},${p.lon}`).join('|');\n  const params = new URLSearchParams({\n    origins: coordStr,\n    destinations: coordStr,\n    mode: 'car',\n    key: apiKey,\n  });\n  const url = `${NB_BASE_URL}${DM_PATH}?${params.toString()}`;\n\n  let json;\n  try {\n    const res = await fetch(url);\n    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`DM ${res.status}`);\n    json = await res.json();\n  } catch (err) {\n    if (log) log(`    circuity: DM call failed (${err.message}) — falling back`);\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  const rows = json.rows || [];\n  let sumNet = 0;\n  let sumStraight = 0;\n  let pairs = 0;\n  for (let i = 0; i < sample.length; i++) {\n    const elements = (rows[i] && rows[i].elements) || [];\n    for (let j = 0; j < sample.length; j++) {\n      if (i === j) continue;\n      const netMeters = elements[j] && elements[j].distance && elements[j].distance.value;\n      if (typeof netMeters !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(netMeters) || netMeters <= 0) continue;\n      const netKm = netMeters / 1000;\n      // Straight-line in the same km space as `nnMed` / cluster distances:\n      // the pipeline's equirectangular projection carried on each POS as\n      // (x, y). Consistent with what CIRCUITY multiplies against.\n      const straightKm = Math.hypot(sample[i].x - sample[j].x, sample[i].y - sample[j].y);\n      if (straightKm < MIN_PAIR_KM) continue;\n      sumNet += netKm;\n      sumStraight += straightKm;\n      pairs++;\n    }\n  }\n  if (pairs < 5 || sumStraight <= 0) return null;\n  const ratio = sumNet / sumStraight;\n  // Bound the ratio to a sane band. Below 1 means the API returned\n  // shortcuts that can't beat straight lines (broken/incomplete data);\n  // above 3 means we sampled far-apart POS with a bridge/river detour\n  // that isn't representative of within-territory travel.\n  if (ratio < 1.0 || ratio > 3.0) return null;\n  return ratio;\n}\n\n/** Measure per-territory circuity for every territory in parallel.\n *  Returns Float64Array of length R with either the empirical ratio or\n *  the caller's fallback for territories that failed / were too small. */\nasync function measureTerritoryCircuities(pos, R, apiKey, fallback, log) {\n  const byT = Array.from({length: R}, () => []);\n  for (const p of pos) byT[p.terr].push(p);\n  const out = new Float64Array(R);\n  await Promise.all(\n    byT.map(async (pts, t) => {\n      const r = await measureTerritoryCircuity(pts, apiKey, log);\n      out[t] = r == null ? fallback : r;\n      if (log) {\n        log(\n          `    territory ${String(t + 1).padStart(2)} circuity=` +\n            `${out[t].toFixed(2)}${r == null ? ' (fallback)' : ''}` +\n            ` (${pts.length} POS)`,\n        );\n      }\n    }),\n  );\n  return out;\n}\n\nmodule.exports = {measureTerritoryCircuity, measureTerritoryCircuities};\n"
}

Absent / failed calls fall back per-territory. */\nasync function buildTerritories(pos, log, options = {}) {\n  const {apiKey} = options;\n  const caps = {\n    week: CFG.WEEKLY_CAP_H * CFG.WEEK_CAP_FACTOR,\n    day2: 2 * CFG.DAILY_CAP_H * CFG.DAY2_FACTOR,\n    day4: 4 * CFG.DAILY_CAP_H * CFG.DAY4_FACTOR,\n    mt: 2 * CFG.DAILY_CAP_H * CFG.MT_FACTOR,\n  };\n  // initial travel estimate: 2 min/visit\n  for (const p of pos) { p.travelH = 2 / 60; p.visitH = p.tempoH + p.travelH; p.weekH = p.freq * p.visitH; }\n  let totalH = pos.reduce((a, p) => a + p.weekH, 0);\n  let R = Math.ceil(totalH / (CFG.WEEKLY_CAP_H * CFG.UTIL_TARGET));\n  log(`initial estimate: ${totalH.toFixed(0)} h/week -> ${R} territories`);\n  let cents = await balancedCluster(pos, R, caps, log);\n  for (let loop = 0; loop < 4; loop++) {\n    recomputeTravel(pos, R);\n    totalH = pos.reduce((a, p) => a + p.weekH, 0);\n    const Rn = Math.ceil(totalH / (CFG.WEEKLY_CAP_H * CFG.UTIL_TARGET));\n    log(`loop ${loop}: total ${totalH.toFixed(0)} h/week -> R=${Rn}`);\n    if (Rn === R && loop > 0) break;\n    R = Rn;\n    cents = await balancedCluster(pos, R, caps, log);\n  }\n  recomputeTravel(pos, R);\n  // Empirical per-territory circuity from NB Distance Matrix. Done once,\n  // AFTER territories have settled — earlier iterations use CFG.CIRCUITY\n  // as bootstrap so R stabilizes cheaply, then a single round of DM\n  // calls refines the per-territory travel estimate that drives repair\n  // and downstream reporting.\n  let circuityByT = null;\n  if (apiKey) {\n    log('measuring per-territory road circuity via NB Distance Matrix...');\n    circuityByT = await measureTerritoryCircuities(pos, R, apiKey, CFG.CIRCUITY, log);\n    const mean = circuityByT.reduce((a, b) => a + b, 0) / R;\n    log(`  mean measured circuity: ${mean.toFixed(2)} (default ${CFG.CIRCUITY})`);\n    recomputeTravel(pos, R, circuityByT);\n  } else {\n    log('(no API key supplied — using default CIRCUITY for travel estimate)');\n  }\n  repair(pos, cents, R, caps);\n  recomputeTravel(pos, R, circuityByT);\n  repair(pos, cents, R, caps);\n  recomputeTravel(pos, R, circuityByT);\n  return { R, cents, caps, circuityByT };\n}"

### CLAUDE (2026-07-22T18:14:44.182Z)

Clean. Here's what changes on the next pipeline run:

- Once territories settle, the pipeline calls NB `/distancematrix/json` **once per territory** with a deterministic 8-POS sample (~R matrix calls total, run in parallel).
- Each call computes `mean(network km / straight-line km)` across the ~56 non-diagonal pairs and uses that as *that territory's* `circuity` in `travelPerVisitH()`.
- Failed / too-small / out-of-band (< 1.0 or > 3.0) ratios fall back per-territory to `CFG.CIRCUITY = 1.4`, so a bad DM response doesn't poison the whole run.
- No API key on the request → skips DM entirely and behaves exactly as before.

The progress log will show per-territory measurements, e.g.:
```
measuring per-territory road circuity via NB Distance Matrix...
    territory  1 circuity=1.52 (123 POS)
    territory  2 circuity=1.38 (98 POS)
    ...
  mean measured circuity: 1.47 (default 1.4)
```

Structural distance uses (Voronoi boundaries, LP objective, k-means centroids, MILP spatial affinity) still run in the Euclidean km space — as discussed, those need it to work at all.

 "content": "// Client-side preview parser. Mirrors the header-lookup logic in\n// libs/territory-planner/src/parse.js so the browser table shows the\n// same rows the server pipeline will operate on — no round-trip needed\n// to display the preview table. When the user clicks Build the original\n// File is re-uploaded and parseBase runs authoritatively; this parser\n// only exists to power the selection UI.\n\nimport * as XLSX from 'xlsx'\n\nexport interface PreviewRow {\n  matricula: string\n  cep: string\n  tipo: string\n  freq: number\n  tempoDays: number\n  diasAtend: string\n  diaRestr: string\n  lat: number\n  lon: number\n  /** True when the row is a zero-frequency POS that the server pipeline\n   *  will silently drop (matches parse.js excluded-count behavior). */\n  zeroFreq: boolean\n  /** True when LAT_LONG couldn't be parsed. */\n  badCoord: boolean\n}\n\n/** Column headers we accept, in preference order. Same alternate-name\n *  lists as parse.js so an accented and unaccented copy of the same\n *  workbook both resolve. */\nconst COLUMNS = {\n  matricula: ['MATRÍCULA', 'MATRICULA'],\n  cep: ['CEP'],\n  latLong: ['LAT_LONG'],\n  tipo: ['TIPO DE VENDEDOR'],\n  freq: ['FREQUENCIA DE VISITAS', 'FREQUÊNCIA DE VISITAS'],\n  tempo: ['TEMPO NO CLIENTE'],\n  dias: ['DIAS ATENDIMENTO DA CIDADE'],\n  restr: ['DIA RESTRIÇÃO CLIENTE', 'DIA RESTRICAO CLIENTE'],\n} as const\n\ntype ColKey = keyof typeof COLUMNS\n\n/** Normalize a header cell to the uppercase, whitespace-collapsed form\n *  parse.js compares against. */\nfunction normalizeHeader(v: unknown): string {\n  return String(v ?? '').trim().toUpperCase()\n}\n\nexport async function parsePreview(file: File): Promise<PreviewRow[]> {\n  const buf = await file.arrayBuffer()\n  const wb = XLSX.read(buf, {type: 'array'})\n  const sheet = wb.Sheets['Base'] ?? wb.Sheets[wb.SheetNames[0]]\n  if (!sheet) throw new Error('Workbook has no Base sheet')\n\n  // Read as a 2D array so we can locate columns by their exact header\n  // string, matching the server parser instead of trusting sheet_to_json's\n  // header inference (which mangles duplicates and accented names).\n  const grid = XLSX.utils.sheet_to_json<unknown[]>(sheet, {\n    header: 1,\n    defval: '',\n    blankrows: false,\n  })\n  if (grid.length < 2) return []\n\n  const headerRow = grid[0] as unknown[]\n  const colIdx: Record<ColKey, number> = {} as Record<ColKey, number>\n  for (const key of Object.keys(COLUMNS) as ColKey[]) {\n    const wanted = COLUMNS[key]\n    const idx = headerRow.findIndex((h) =>\n      wanted.includes(normalizeHeader(h) as (typeof wanted)[number]),\n    )\n    if (idx < 0) {\n      throw new Error(`Column not found: ${wanted[0]}`)\n    }\n    colIdx[key] = idx\n  }\n\n  const rows: PreviewRow[] = []\n  for (let i = 1; i < grid.length; i++) {\n    const raw = grid[i] as unknown[]\n    const matricula = String(raw[colIdx.matricula] ?? '').trim()\n    if (!matricula) continue\n    const freqRaw = raw[colIdx.freq]\n    const freq = Number(freqRaw)\n    const ll = String(raw[colIdx.latLong] ?? '').split(',')\n    const lat = Number(ll[0])\n    const lon = Number(ll[1])\n    const tempoDays = Number(raw[colIdx.tempo]) || 0\n    rows.push({\n      matricula,\n      cep: String(raw[colIdx.cep] ?? ''),\n      tipo: String(raw[colIdx.tipo] ?? ''),\n      freq: Number.isFinite(freq) ? freq : 0,\n      tempoDays,\n      diasAtend: String(raw[colIdx.dias] ?? ''),\n      diaRestr: String(raw[colIdx.restr] ?? ''),\n      lat,\n      lon,\n      zeroFreq: !freq,\n      badCoord: !Number.isFinite(lat) || !Number.isFinite(lon),\n    })\n  }\n  return rows\n}\n"
}

}
