### CLAUDE (2026-07-22T20:37:12.779Z)

Clean. New flow:

1. **Upload** — user drops the .xlsx. Client parses it in the browser (xlsx.js) → `parsing` phase.
2. **Preview** — full DataGrid of every row with:
   - Search box (POS matrícula)
   - Multi-select filter for `TIPO DE VENDEDOR`
   - Checkbox column, all rows preselected
   - Warning chips on rows that would be dropped anyway (`0-freq`, `bad coord`)
   - Header shows `{selected} of {total} selected`
   - **"Build territories"** button in the top-right (disabled if < 3 valid selected)
   - **"Back"** button returns to upload
3. **Build** — the "Build territories" click POSTs the original file **plus** the `selected` matrícula list (JSON in FormData) to `/api/territory-planner`. Server-side `runPipeline` filters `pos` after `parseBase` to only the selected IDs, then runs clustering/scheduling/boundaries on that subset.
4. **Map** — same map as before, now scoped to the selected POS.

Guards:
- Server rejects `< 3` selected POS with a clear error.
- Filters hide rows but preserve selection state (`keepNonExistentRowsSelected`) so toggling a filter off restores prior picks.
- Bad-coord rows are removed from the selection before submit to avoid tripping the server-side "no feasible visit pattern" abort.

All 41 territory-planner strings translated across 5 locales.

The current code builds per-territory alpha-shapes (only triangles with all edges < ~5× median-nearest-neighbor) then Voronoi-clips against them, which is exactly what creates the "blob per neighborhood" look. Simplest way to a single contiguous polygon per territory is a convex hull of the territory's POS.

 "content": "'use strict';\n// d3-delaunay is ESM-only; imported dynamically so Next's webpack (which\n// can't resolve ESM through require()) leaves it as a runtime external —\n// see `serverComponentsExternalPackages` in the app's next.config.js.\nconst CFG = require('./config');\n\n/** Non-overlapping territory boundary polygons (in km space -> lon/lat GeoJSON).\n *\n *  One contiguous polygon per territory. We use the convex hull of the\n *  territory's POS (after excluding far-outlier geocodes) so:\n *    - the shape is always a single Polygon, never a MultiPolygon;\n *    - internal gaps between POS neighborhoods are bridged instead of\n *      producing separate blobs the way the earlier Voronoi + per-territory\n *      alpha-shape rendering did.\n *  Adjacent territories may overlap where their POS interleave — that's an\n *  intentional trade for guaranteed contiguity; the semi-transparent fill\n *  in the deck.gl layer lets both colors show through.\n *\n *  A degenerate territory (<3 POS, or all collinear) still gets an entry so\n *  the color legend stays honest; we render it as a small circle around the\n *  centroid.\n */\nasync function buildBoundaries(pos, R, proj) {\n  const { Delaunay } = await import('d3-delaunay');\n\n  // Exclude far geocode outliers per territory before hulling — a single\n  // 100 km outlier POS would balloon the whole hull. Same rule as the\n  // earlier renderer.\n  const cx = new Float64Array(R);\n  const cy = new Float64Array(R);\n  const cn = new Float64Array(R);\n  for (const p of pos) {\n    cx[p.terr] += p.x;\n    cy[p.terr] += p.y;\n    cn[p.terr]++;\n  }\n  for (let r = 0; r < R; r++) {\n    if (cn[r]) { cx[r] /= cn[r]; cy[r] /= cn[r]; }\n  }\n\n  const byT = Array.from({length: R}, () => []);\n  for (const p of pos) {\n    if (Math.hypot(p.x - cx[p.terr], p.y - cy[p.terr]) <= CFG.OUTLIER_KM) {\n      byT[p.terr].push(p);\n    }\n  }\n\n  const features = [];\n  for (let t = 0; t < R; t++) {\n    const pts = byT[t];\n    if (!pts.length) continue;\n\n    let ringKm;\n    if (pts.length >= 3) {\n      ringKm = hullRing(pts, Delaunay);\n    }\n    if (!ringKm || ringKm.length < 4) {\n      // Fewer than 3 usable POS (or degenerate/collinear layout) —\n      // fall back to a small circle around the centroid so the\n      // territory still shows up on the map.\n      ringKm = circleRing(cx[t], cy[t], 0.5);\n    }\n\n    // Convert km -> lon/lat via the pipeline's equirectangular projection\n    // (same round-trip as before), then re-wrap as a single Polygon so\n    // downstream consumers get one contiguous piece.\n    const ringLL = ringKm.map(([x, y]) => [\n      Number((proj.lon0 + x / proj.kx).toFixed(7)),\n      Number((proj.lat0 + y / proj.ky).toFixed(7)),\n    ]);\n\n    features.push({\n      type: 'Feature',\n      properties: {terr: t},\n      geometry: {type: 'Polygon', coordinates: [ringLL]},\n    });\n  }\n  return {type: 'FeatureCollection', features};\n}\n\n/** Convex hull of a POS set, returned as a closed ring of [x, y] pairs\n *  in km space. Uses d3-delaunay's hull (CCW indices into the point list). */\nfunction hullRing(pts, Delaunay) {\n  const del = Delaunay.from(pts.map((p) => [p.x, p.y]));\n  const hull = del.hull; // Uint32Array of point indices, CCW\n  if (!hull || hull.length < 3) return null;\n  const ring = [];\n  for (const i of hull) ring.push([pts[i].x, pts[i].y]);\n  ring.push(ring[0]);\n  return ring;\n}\n\n/** Closed 24-gon around (cx, cy) with radius r, in km space. */\nfunction circleRing(cx, cy, r, n = 24) {\n  const ring = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i <= n; i++) {\n    const a = (2 * Math.PI * i) / n;\n    ring.push([cx + r * Math.cos(a), cy + r * Math.sin(a)]);\n  }\n  return ring;\n}\n\nmodule.exports = {buildBoundaries};\n"

### CLAUDE (2026-07-22T20:50:00.148Z)

Clean. Boundaries are now built as a **convex hull per territory** — one contiguous `Polygon` feature per territory, no more per-neighborhood blobs.

Trade-offs to expect:
- **Guaranteed contiguity**: every territory is a single hull.
- **Overlap**: where territories interleave spatially, their hulls will overlap. The deck.gl fill is at 50/255 alpha so both colors show through; the darker border stays per-territory.
- **Coastal territories**: the hull extends across the coastline gaps (some polygon will cover water where POS trace the coast). If that becomes visually noisy, we can swap to a concave hull (larger alpha-shape) — same code shape, just a smarter hull function.
- **Outlier trimming preserved**: POS more than 25 km from their territory centroid are still excluded before hulling so a single bad geocode doesn't balloon the polygon.
- **Degenerate territories** (< 3 POS or collinear) render as a small circle around their centroid so the legend stays honest.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-22T20:54:14.625Z)

This error is not from the territory-planner code — the failing `fetch` at `fetcher-rsc.ts:66` is in `libs/common/src/lib/components/common-layout/common-layout-rsc.tsx:30`, a shared RSC that runs in the layout tree of every page in the app. It's calling the BFF at `https://bff-staging-[GCP_PROJECT_NUMBER].us-central1.run.app/common/api_keys` from your `.env.local`.

I just curled that URL directly and it responds normally (403 without auth in ~137ms — the connection is fine). So the BFF isn't down; the fetch failed transiently on your dev server. Two things typically cause this in local dev:

1. **HMR / fast-refresh timing.** I've been editing files rapidly; Next dev re-renders the layout after each edit, and the RSC fetches fire again. If one races with a dev-server restart or a stale request, it errors. The error persists in the overlay until dismissed.
2. **The pipeline blocks Node's event loop.** HiGHS WASM (MILP) and polygon-clipping do multi-second synchronous compute. During that window a concurrent RSC render can't complete its outbound fetch and errors out.

Quick things to try:
- Dismiss the overlay (X), hard-refresh (⌘⇧R), and try Build again.
- If it fails again mid-run: check the terminal running `nx serve route-planner-v2` — the BFF error there will have a real cause (ECONNRESET, timeout, etc.). Paste it and I can help.

If it keeps happening reliably right at Build click (not mid-pipeline), it's very likely (2) — the fix is moving `runPipeline` to a worker thread so the pipeline can't block the main event loop. That's ~30 lines of change; say the word and I'll do it.

See `serverComponentsExternalPackages` in the app's next.config.js.\nconst { medianNN } = require('./geo');\nconst CFG = require('./config');\n\nconst circle = (x, y, r, n = 12) => {\n  const ring = [];\n  for (let i = 0; i <= n; i++) {\n    const a = (2 * Math.PI * i) / n;\n    ring.push([x + r * Math.cos(a), y + r * Math.sin(a)]);\n  }\n  return [[ring]];\n};\nconst triPoly = (a, b, c) => [[[a, b, c, a]]];\n\n/** Non-overlapping territory boundary polygons (in km space -> lon/lat GeoJSON).\n *  Voronoi cells per POS unioned by territory, clipped to an alpha-shape coverage region. */\nasync function buildBoundaries(pos, R, proj) {\n  const { Delaunay } = await import('d3-delaunay');\n  const pcMod = await import('polygon-clipping');\n  const pc = pcMod.default || pcMod;\n  // exclude far geocode outliers\n  const cx = new Float64Array(R), cy = new Float64Array(R), cn = new Float64Array(R);\n  for (const p of pos) { cx[p.terr] += p.x; cy[p.terr] += p.y; cn[p.terr]++; }\n  for (let r = 0; r < R; r++) { cx[r] /= cn[r]; cy[r] /= cn[r]; }\n  const core = pos.filter((p) => Math.hypot(p.x - cx[p.terr], p.y - cy[p.terr]) <= CFG.OUTLIER_KM);\n\n  // coverage region: union of per-territory alpha shapes\n  let regionParts = [];\n  for (let t = 0; t < R; t++) {\n    const pts = core.filter((p) => p.terr === t);\n    if (!pts.length) continue;\n    const thresh = Math.max(1.0, 5 * medianNN(pts));\n    const polys = pts.map((p) => circle(p.x, p.y, 0.3));\n    if (pts.length >= 4) {\n      const del = Delaunay.from(pts.map((p) => [p.x, p.y]));\n      const { triangles } = del;\n      for (let i = 0; i < triangles.length; i += 3) {\n        const a = pts[triangles[i]], b = pts[triangles[i + 1]], c = pts[triangles[i + 2]];\n        const e = Math.max(Math.hypot(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y),\n          Math.hypot(b.x - c.x, b.y - c.y), Math.hypot(c.x - a.x, c.y - a.y));\n        if (e < thresh) polys.push(triPoly([a.x, a.y], [b.x, b.y], [c.x, c.y]));\n      }\n    }\n    regionParts.push(pc.union(...polys));\n  }\n  const region = pc.union(...regionParts);\n\n  // Voronoi partition (dedupe near-identical coords)\n  const seen = new Map();\n  const uniq = [];\n  for (const p of core) {\n    const k = `${p.x.toFixed(4)},${p.y.toFixed(4)}`;\n    if (!seen.has(k)) { seen.set(k, true); uniq.push(p); }\n  }\n  const del = Delaunay.from(uniq.map((p) => [p.x, p.y]));\n  const xs = uniq.map((p) => p.x), ys = uniq.map((p) => p.y);\n  const pad = 50;\n  const vor = del.voronoi([Math.min(...xs) - pad, Math.min(...ys) - pad,\n    Math.max(...xs) + pad, Math.max(...ys) + pad]);\n  const cellsByTerr = Array.from({ length: R }, () => []);\n  uniq.forEach((p, i) => {\n    const cell = vor.cellPolygon(i);\n    if (cell) cellsByTerr[p.terr].push([[cell]]);\n  });\n\n  const features = [];\n  for (let t = 0; t < R; t++) {\n    if (!cellsByTerr[t].length) continue;\n    const merged = pc.union(...cellsByTerr[t]);\n    const clipped = pc.intersection(merged, region);\n    const coords = clipped.map((poly) => poly.map((ring) =>\n      ring.map(([x, y]) => [\n        Number((proj.lon0 + x / proj.kx).toFixed(7)),\n        Number((proj.lat0 + y / proj.ky).toFixed(7)),\n      ])));\n    features.push({ type: 'Feature', properties: { terr: t },\n      geometry: { type: 'MultiPolygon', coordinates: coords } });\n  }\n  return { type: 'FeatureCollection', features };\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { buildBoundaries };\n"

 "content": "// Client-side per-territory convex hulls, packaged as the same\n// FeatureCollection shape the server emits for Voronoi boundaries so\n// the map's GeoJsonLayer can swap between the two without other changes.\n//\n// Not pipeline-quality — the hull is computed directly in lon/lat with\n// Andrew's monotone-chain algorithm. That's approximate over large\n// spans (WGS84 isn't planar) but for territory visualization at metro\n// scale the distortion is invisible.\n\nimport type {TerritoryBoundaries, TerritoryPos} from './types'\n\ntype Pt = [number, number]\n\n/** 2D cross product (o→a) × (o→b). Positive = left turn (CCW). */\nfunction cross(o: Pt, a: Pt, b: Pt): number {\n  return (a[0] - o[0]) * (b[1] - o[1]) - (a[1] - o[1]) * (b[0] - o[0])\n}\n\n/** Andrew's monotone chain — O(n log n). Returns a closed CCW ring in\n *  [lon, lat] order. Handles collinear/duplicate points by discarding\n *  them via the `<= 0` guard. */\nfunction convexHull(points: Pt[]): Pt[] {\n  if (points.length < 3) {\n    const closed = points.slice()\n    if (closed.length > 0) closed.push(closed[0])\n    return closed\n  }\n  const sorted = points\n    .slice()\n    .sort((a, b) => (a[0] === b[0] ? a[1] - b[1] : a[0] - b[0]))\n  const lower: Pt[] = []\n  for (const p of sorted) {\n    while (\n      lower.length >= 2 &&\n      cross(lower[lower.length - 2], lower[lower.length - 1], p) <= 0\n    ) {\n      lower.pop()\n    }\n    lower.push(p)\n  }\n  const upper: Pt[] = []\n  for (let i = sorted.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) {\n    const p = sorted[i]\n    while (\n      upper.length >= 2 &&\n      cross(upper[upper.length - 2], upper[upper.length - 1], p) <= 0\n    ) {\n      upper.pop()\n    }\n    upper.push(p)\n  }\n  // Concatenate, dropping the duplicate join points, then close the ring.\n  lower.pop()\n  upper.pop()\n  const ring = lower.concat(upper)\n  ring.push(ring[0])\n  return ring\n}\n\nexport function computeHullBoundaries(\n  pos: TerritoryPos[],\n): TerritoryBoundaries {\n  const byT = new Map<number, Pt[]>()\n  for (const p of pos) {\n    const arr = byT.get(p.terr) ?? []\n    arr.push([p.lon, p.lat])\n    if (arr.length === 1) byT.set(p.terr, arr)\n  }\n  const features: TerritoryBoundaries['features'] = []\n  const terrIds = [...byT.keys()].sort((a, b) => a - b)\n  for (const terr of terrIds) {\n    const pts = byT.get(terr)!\n    if (pts.length === 0) continue\n    const ring = convexHull(pts)\n    if (ring.length < 4) continue // Degenerate — skip to keep GeoJSON valid.\n    features.push({\n      type: 'Feature',\n      properties: {terr},\n      // Wrap the single hull as a MultiPolygon so the type + GeoJsonLayer\n      // pipeline is identical to the server's Voronoi output.\n      geometry: {type: 'MultiPolygon', coordinates: [[ring]]},\n    })\n  }\n  return {type: 'FeatureCollection', features}\n}\n"

### CLAUDE (2026-07-23T17:20:43.044Z)

Here's a map of the hardcoded knobs, grouped by how much a planner user would actually want to touch them. All live in `libs/territory-planner/src/config.js` (plus a couple in `matrix.js`).

## Tier 1 — Planner-facing (worth exposing first)

These directly answer "how much can a rep do?" — a sales manager would want to override them per-market.

| Param | Value | What it controls |
|---|---|---|
| `DAILY_CAP_H` | 7.42 h | Hours per rep per day (on-route) |
| `WEEKLY_CAP_H` | 37.08 h | Hours per rep per week |
| `UTIL_TARGET` | 0.93 | Planned utilization → drives rep count `R = ceil(totalH / (WEEKLY_CAP_H · UTIL_TARGET))` |
| `SPEED_KMH` | 25 | Assumed urban travel speed |
| `CIRCUITY` | 1.4 | Road/straight-line ratio (used as fallback when NB DM off/fails) |
| `OUTLIER_KM` | 25 | Distance from centroid before a POS is flagged as an outlier |

## Tier 2 — Cycle shape (usually market-specific)

These bake in the FEMSA week/day model. A different customer will want a different shape.

| Param | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `WEEKS` | `[1,2,3,4]` | Cycle length |
| `DAYS` | `[2..6]` Mon–Fri | Working days (7 = Sat is excluded) |
| `DAY_PAIRS` | 5 spaced pairs | Allowable Mon/Wed, Mon/Thu, etc. for freq-2 POS |
| `CLS_MAP` | `{23456:0, 2356:1, 25:2, 36:3}` | Day-availability classes keyed off DIAS ATENDIMENTO — very FEMSA-specific |
| `DAY_NAMES` / `DAY_SHORT` | pt/en mix | Labels shown in reports |

## Tier 3 — Safety-margin factors (advanced)

Currently tuned to leave headroom in the LP. Rarely retuned but useful for stress-testing.

| Param | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `DAY2_FACTOR` | 0.90 | Margin on 2-workable-day class caps |
| `DAY4_FACTOR` | 0.94 | Margin on 4-workable-day class caps |
| `MT_FACTOR` | 0.96 | Margin on structural Mon+Thu bound |
| `WEEK_CAP_FACTOR` | 0.98 | Repair target vs weekly capacity |

## Tier 4 — Solver knobs (dev-only, don't ship to end users)

Correctness/perf trade-offs. Leave in code.

| Param | Value | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `GRID_KM` | 0.35 | LP aggregation cell size (coarser = faster, less precise) |
| `SPATIAL_W` | 0.0002 | Spatial-affinity weight in scheduling MILP |
| `MILP_TIME` / `MILP_RETRY_TIME` | 60 / 300 s | Per-territory MILP time budget |
| `MILP_GAP` | 0.01 | MIP relative gap tolerance |
| Loop counts: `25` in `balancedCluster`, `4000` in `repair`, outer `4` in `buildTerritories` | | Iteration caps |
| `matrix.js`: `SAMPLE_PER_TERR=8`, `MIN_PAIR_KM=0.5`, ratio bounds `[1.0, 3.0]` | | NB DM sampling behavior |

## Recommendation

If you want to add a "settings" panel on the upload/preview page, start with Tier 1 — those six values are the ones that change the answer in ways a planner would recognize. Everything else I'd leave as `CFG` defaults with an optional `overrides?: Partial<TerritoryConfig>` on `runPipeline()` so power users can pass them in, without polluting the UI.

### CLAUDE (2026-07-23T17:35:16.439Z)

Done. Summary of what shipped:

**Preview toolbar** — new `⚙ Settings` icon button sits between the selection counter and the **Build territories** button. Popover has three numeric fields (Daily cap h, Weekly cap h, Utilization target 0–1) with placeholders showing the pipeline defaults (7.42 / 37.08 / 0.93). Blank field = use default. Small badge on the button shows how many overrides are active. Reset button clears them. Values persist through the round-trip to the map and back via the same lifted `previewState` used by search/filter/selection.

**Wire-up** — client serializes non-blank fields into a JSON `overrides` form field. The API route validates them (positive finite, util ≤ 1) and forwards to `runPipeline(..., {overrides})`. The pipeline (`cluster.js`, `schedule.js`, `validate.js`) now takes those three values in place of the CFG constants — affects rep count sizing, transportation-LP caps, repair caps, MILP daily-slot cap, over-cap validation, and the reported `dailyCapH` metric so the sidebar shows the value that was actually used.

**Types** — new `TerritoryPipelineOverrides` exported from `@ncc/territory-planner`.

**i18n** — 10 new keys across en / es-MX / fr-CA / pl-PL / pt-BR.

Files changed:
- `libs/territory-planner/src/{cluster.js:191, schedule.js:8, validate.js:5, run.js:32, index.ts}`

### USER (2026-07-23T17:39:04.113Z)

Is there something that controls the number of sales reps being considered when building the territories


### CLAUDE (2026-07-23T17:39:21.428Z)

Not directly — the rep count `R` is **derived**, not set. Look at `libs/territory-planner/src/cluster.js:202`:

```js
R = Math.ceil(totalH / (weeklyCap * utilTarget))
```

So the number of reps is a function of three things:

1. **`totalH`** — sum of `weekH` across all selected POS. Driven by your POS selection (filter + checkbox in the preview table), each POS's `freq × (tempoH + travelH)`.
2. **`weeklyCap`** — hours per rep per week. Already exposed via the new Settings panel.
3. **`utilTarget`** — planned utilization (0–1). Already exposed via the new Settings panel.

The loop at `cluster.js:205-213` re-runs this after refining travel-time estimates, so `R` can grow/shrink by 1–2 as travel is recomputed, then stabilizes.

### Indirect control today
You can already move `R` up or down via Settings:
- Higher `WEEKLY_CAP_H` or `UTIL_TARGET` → fewer reps
- Lower either → more reps
- Narrower POS selection → fewer reps

### If you want a direct knob
Two options, easy to add:

| Option | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **`targetR`** (pin) | Skip the `ceil(...)` formula, use exactly N territories. Solver may fail if N is too small for the workload. |
| **`minR` / `maxR`** (clamp) | Compute R as today, then clamp. Safe fallback — gives the manager a floor/ceiling without breaking feasibility. |

The clamp approach is safer and matches how a manager typically thinks ("I have 12 reps hired — plan for 10 to 14"). Want me to add either?


### USER (2026-07-23T17:40:05.024Z)

so if my solution says '27 Territories' that would be 27 rep assignments?


### CLAUDE (2026-07-23T17:40:18.881Z)

Yes — 1 territory = 1 rep in this model. They're the same unit.

The clustering step assigns each POS to exactly one territory, and each territory's total weekly hours are bounded by the per-rep capacity (`weeklyCap × utilTarget`). The scheduling step then builds a 4-week Mon–Fri visit calendar for that one rep. So "27 Territories" means the pipeline sized the workload at 27 rep assignments, each with:

- ~37 h/week of on-route work (before utilization)
- Its own geographic footprint (the Voronoi/Hull polygon on the map)
- Its own 4-week × 5-day visit schedule

If you have, say, 25 reps hired and the pipeline returns 27, the interpretation is: at the current capacity/utilization settings, this POS set needs 2 more reps than you have — either hire, raise `UTIL_TARGET`, raise `WEEKLY_CAP_H`, or drop some POS from the plan.

Payload is intentionally minimal — one vehicle with no\n// fixed start/end index (the optimizer picks both), one job per stop.\n//\n// Response is shaped for the map/grid: decoded polyline coordinates\n// plus one row per stop with cumulative arrival time and per-leg\n// distance/duration.\n//\n// POST body (application/json):\n//   {\n//     description?: string,\n//     dateISO: string,               // YYYY-MM-DD, used to timestamp arrivals\n//     stops: Array<{\n//       matricula: string,\n//       lat: number,\n//       lon: number,\n//       serviceSeconds: number,\n//     }>,\n//   }\n//\n// Response body (200):\n//   {\n//     coordinates: Array<[lon, lat]>,     // decoded route polyline\n//     totalDistanceM: number,\n//     totalDurationS: number,\n//     totalServiceS: number,\n//     startUnixS: number,\n//     stops: Array<{\n//       sequence: number,               // 1-based\n//       matricula: string,\n//       lat: number,\n//       lon: number,\n//       arrivalUnixS: number,\n//       serviceSeconds: number,\n//       legDistanceM: number,           // 0 for the first stop\n//       cumulativeDistanceM: number,\n//       cumulativeDurationS: number,\n//     }>,\n//   }\n\nimport type {NextRequest} from 'next/server'\n\nexport const runtime = 'nodejs'\nexport const maxDuration = 60\n\nconst NB_HOST = 'https://api.nextbillion.io'\nconst POST_PATH = '/optimise-mvrp'\nconst RESULT_PATH = '/optimise-mvrp/result'\n// Retrieved results tend to arrive in well under a second for a single\n// vehicle & a couple of dozen jobs, but we still cap the poll budget\n// so a stuck job doesn't hold the route open indefinitely.\nconst POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 800\nconst POLL_TIMEOUT_MS = 45_000\n\ninterface StopIn {\n  matricula: string\n  lat: number\n  lon: number\n  serviceSeconds: number\n}\n\nexport async function POST(request: NextRequest) {\n  const apiKey = readCookie(request, 'apikey')\n  if (!apiKey) {\n    return Response.json(\n      {error: 'No API key selected. Choose one from the header dropdown.'},\n      {status: 400},\n    )\n  }\n\n  let body: {\n    description?: string\n    dateISO?: string\n    stops?: StopIn[]\n  }\n  try {\n    body = await request.json()\n  } catch {\n    return Response.json({error: 'invalid JSON body'}, {status: 400})\n  }\n\n  const stops = Array.isArray(body.stops) ? body.stops : []\n  if (stops.length < 2) {\n    return Response.json(\n      {error: 'need at least 2 stops to run a TSP'},\n      {status: 400},\n    )\n  }\n  if (stops.length > 500) {\n    // /optimise-mvrp handles more than this, but for a single-rep day\n    // we should never come close — surface a clear error rather than\n    // shipping a request that costs a lot and probably signals a bug.\n    return Response.json(\n      {error: `too many stops (${stops.length})`},\n      {status: 400},\n    )\n  }\n\n  // Route arrivals report unix seconds. ### CLAUDE (2026-07-24T13:25:01.075Z)

Typecheck clean on all touched files.

Summary of the new feature:

**Trigger** — When the user has exactly 1 territory selected in the Territories dropdown AND exactly 1 day picked on the calendar (click the same day twice, or just click once), the map automatically fires a TSP request. Changing either input aborts the in-flight request and queues a fresh one.

**Server** — new `POST /route-planner/api/territory-planner/route` proxies to NB `/optimise-mvrp` (v1). Payload is minimal: one vehicle with no fixed start/end (`start_index`/`end_index` omitted → optimizer picks both), one job per POS with `service = tempoH × 3600` seconds. API key pulled from the `apikey` cookie. POST + poll (`/optimise-mvrp/result`, 800 ms interval, 45 s budget). Response is reshaped into `{coordinates, stops[]}` with cumulative distance/time per stop; the polyline5 geometry is decoded inline.

**Polyline** — new `PathLayer` (deck.gl) drawn above the ScatterplotLayer in dark blue (`rgba(30,64,175,220)`) when a route is ready.

**Bottom grid** — floating panel across the bottom of the map. Header shows `Territory N · Fri, Mar 5 · 8 stops · 42.3 km total · 3h 20m`. Sticky-header table with columns: `#`, `POS`, `Arrival` (local HH:MM), `Service`, `Leg`, `Cum. dist`, `Cum. time`. Same panel doubles as a loading/error banner and as a "not enough stops" hint (needs ≥2 stops).

**Files touched**
- `apps/route-planner-v2/app/api/territory-planner/route/route.ts` (new)
- `apps/route-planner-v2/app/territory-planner/territory-map.tsx`

 "file_path": "/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-[USER]-workspace-ncc/92d5fce2-7c47-4443-8631-1d6a2567eeaa/scratchpad/add_tw_columns.js",
 "content": "// Add two columns (start_tw_1, end_tw_2) to the FEMSA base workbook.\n// Values depend on TIPO DE VENDEDOR (col D):\n//   VEND. NOTURNO         → 15:00 / 22:00\n//   anything else         → 07:30 / 16:30\n// Writes back to the same path.\n\nconst ExcelJS = require('exceljs')\n\nconst PATH =\n  '/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/apps/route-planner/public/FEMSA_-_BASE_POC_FASE_2.xlsx'\n\nconst NOTURNO = 'VEND. NOTURNO'\nconst DAY = {start: '07:30', end: '16:30'}\nconst NIGHT = {start: '15:00', end: '22:00'}\n\n;(async () => {\n  const wb = new ExcelJS.Workbook()\n  await wb.xlsx.readFile(PATH)\n  const sheet = wb.getWorksheet('Base')\n  if (!sheet) throw new Error('Base sheet not found')\n\n  const headerRow = sheet.getRow(1)\n  const tipoCol = 4 // TIPO DE VENDEDOR — verified from inspection\n  const startTwCol = 9\n  const endTwCol = 10\n\n  headerRow.getCell(startTwCol).value = 'start_tw_1'\n  headerRow.getCell(endTwCol).value = 'end_tw_2'\n  headerRow.commit()\n\n  let dayCount = 0\n  let nightCount = 0\n  for (let r = 2; r <= sheet.rowCount; r++) {\n    const row = sheet.getRow(r)\n    const tipoRaw = row.getCell(tipoCol).value\n    if (tipoRaw == null) continue\n    const tipo = String(tipoRaw).trim()\n    const tw = tipo === NOTURNO ? NIGHT : DAY\n    row.getCell(startTwCol).value = tw.start\n    row.getCell(endTwCol).value = tw.end\n    if (tipo === NOTURNO) nightCount++\n    else dayCount++\n    row.commit()\n  }\n\n  await wb.xlsx.writeFile(PATH)\n  console.log(`wrote ${PATH}`)\n  console.log(`  day rows:   ${dayCount}`)\n  console.log(`  night rows: ${nightCount}`)\n})().catch((e) => {\n  console.error(e)\n  process.exit(1)\n})\n"
}

 "new_string": "// Normalize a time-of-day cell to \"HH:MM\". Excel cells may arrive as:\n//   - a plain string like \"07:30\" (what add_tw_columns.js writes),\n//   - a JS Date (when Excel type-inferred the cell as a time), or\n//   - a fractional-day number in [0,1).\n// Returns null for anything unrecognizable so the caller can decide\n// whether to fall back to an unbounded window.\nfunction normalizeHm(v) {\n  if (v === null || v === undefined || v === '') return null;\n  if (typeof v === 'string') {\n    const m = /^(\\d{1,2}):(\\d{2})$/.exec(v.trim());\n    if (!m) return null;\n    const h = Number(m[1]);\n    const mn = Number(m[2]);\n    if (h < 0 || h > 23 || mn < 0 || mn > 59) return null;\n    return `${String(h).padStart(2, '0')}:${String(mn).padStart(2, '0')}`;\n  }\n  if (v instanceof Date) {\n    return `${String(v.getUTCHours()).padStart(2, '0')}:${String(v.getUTCMinutes()).padStart(2, '0')}`;\n  }\n  if (typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v)) {\n    const frac = ((v % 1) + 1) % 1;\n    const total = Math.round(frac * 24 * 60);\n    const h = Math.floor(total / 60);\n    const mn = total % 60;\n    return `${String(h).padStart(2, '0')}:${String(mn).padStart(2, '0')}`;\n  }\n  return null;\n}\n\nfunction parseDaySet(v) {"
}

 "old_string": "/** BHH travel allowance per visit (hours) for a territory's POS set.\n *  `circuity` overrides CFG.CIRCUITY — used by the cluster stage to\n *  plug in a per-territory ratio measured from NB Distance Matrix. */\nfunction travelPerVisitH(pts, weeklyVisits, circuity) {\n  const nDay = Math.max(weeklyVisits / 5, 1);\n  const nnMed = Math.min(Math.max(medianNN(pts), 0.03), 2.0);\n  const cir = typeof circuity === 'number' && isFinite(circuity) ? circuity : CFG.CIRCUITY;\n  const km = cir * 0.7 * (nnMed / 0.48) * Math.sqrt(pts.length / nDay);\n  return km / CFG.SPEED_KMH;\n}",
 "new_string": "/** BHH travel allowance per visit (hours) for a territory's POS set.\n *  `circuity` overrides CFG.CIRCUITY — used by the cluster stage to\n *  plug in a per-territory ratio measured from NB Distance Matrix.\n *  `speedKmh` overrides CFG.SPEED_KMH — surfaced as a user-tunable\n *  setting so different markets can plug in their own assumption. */\nfunction travelPerVisitH(pts, weeklyVisits, circuity, speedKmh) {\n  const nDay = Math.max(weeklyVisits / 5, 1);\n  const nnMed = Math.min(Math.max(medianNN(pts), 0.03), 2.0);\n  const cir = typeof circuity === 'number' && isFinite(circuity) ? circuity : CFG.CIRCUITY;\n  const spd = typeof speedKmh === 'number' && isFinite(speedKmh) && speedKmh > 0\n    ? speedKmh\n    : CFG.SPEED_KMH;\n  const km = cir * 0.7 * (nnMed / 0.48) * Math.sqrt(pts.length / nDay);\n  return km / spd;\n}"
}

Blank strings drop out so\n *  the pipeline sees only fields the user actually overrode. */\nexport function serializeSettings(\n  s: TerritorySettings,\n): {dailyCapH?: number; weeklyCapH?: number; utilTarget?: number} | null {\n  const out: {dailyCapH?: number; weeklyCapH?: number; utilTarget?: number} = {}\n  const daily = parseFloat(s.dailyCapH)\n  const weekly = parseFloat(s.weeklyCapH)\n  const util = parseFloat(s.utilTarget)\n  if (Number.isFinite(daily) && daily > 0) out.dailyCapH = daily\n  if (Number.isFinite(weekly) && weekly > 0) out.weeklyCapH = weekly\n  if (Number.isFinite(util) && util > 0 && util <= 1) out.utilTarget = util\n  return Object.keys(out).length ? out : null\n}",

Kept here as\n *  input placeholders so the user can see what the defaults are without\n *  digging through the pipeline source. */\nexport const SETTINGS_DEFAULTS = {\n  dailyCapH: 7.42,\n  weeklyCapH: 37.08,\n  utilTarget: 0.93,\n  speedKmh: 25,\n}\n\n/** Turn the string-valued input state into the JSON the API route\n *  expects. Blank strings drop out so the pipeline sees only fields\n *  the user actually overrode. */\nexport function serializeSettings(s: TerritorySettings): {\n  dailyCapH?: number\n  weeklyCapH?: number\n  utilTarget?: number\n  speedKmh?: number\n} | null {\n  const out: {\n    dailyCapH?: number\n    weeklyCapH?: number\n    utilTarget?: number\n    speedKmh?: number\n  } = {}\n  const daily = parseFloat(s.dailyCapH)\n  const weekly = parseFloat(s.weeklyCapH)\n  const util = parseFloat(s.utilTarget)\n  const speed = parseFloat(s.speedKmh)\n  if (Number.isFinite(daily) && daily > 0) out.dailyCapH = daily\n  if (Number.isFinite(weekly) && weekly > 0) out.weeklyCapH = weekly\n  if (Number.isFinite(util) && util > 0 && util <= 1) out.utilTarget = util\n  if (Number.isFinite(speed) && speed > 0) out.speedKmh = speed\n  return Object.keys(out).length ? out : null\n}"

### CLAUDE (2026-07-24T17:15:11.542Z)

The numbers are consistent — the label is what's misleading.

- **Weekly workload = 63 h** is the sum of `weekH` across **all POS**, i.e. the total demand for the whole operation. Per rep = 63 / 2 territories = **31.5 h**, which is under the 37.08 h cap ✓.
- **Max rep-day = 6.87 h** is the highest load in any single (rep, week, day) slot — under the 7.42 h daily cap ✓.

So "Weekly workload" reads like a per-rep number but it's really operation-wide. Two low-risk fixes I can apply:

1. **Rename** to "Total weekly workload" (clearest, one word change).
2. **Add a subtitle** showing the per-rep breakdown: `63 h · 31.5 h per rep`.

Want me to do #2? That's the most informative without inventing new numbers — everything else in the sidebar stays as-is.

 "new_string": "// Discrete color scale for the four FEMSA frequencies. Higher freq =\n// warmer color so the \"high-touch\" stops on the day's route pop first\n// when scanning the map. Anything unrecognized falls back to grey.\nfunction freqColor(freq: number): [number, number, number, number] {\n  if (freq >= 2) return [220, 38, 38, 255] // red-600     — 2/wk\n  if (freq >= 1) return [234, 88, 12, 255] // orange-600  — 1/wk\n  if (freq >= 0.5) return [37, 99, 235, 255] // blue-600  — 0.5/wk\n  if (freq > 0) return [22, 163, 74, 255] // green-600   — 0.25/wk\n  return [107, 114, 128, 255] // gray-500 fallback\n}\n\nfunction FreqLegend({stops}: {stops: TspRouteStop[]}) {\n  // Only show swatches for freqs that actually appear on this route so\n  // a single-freq day doesn't render four irrelevant chips.\n  const present = new Set(stops.map((s) => normalizeFreq(s.freq)))\n  const entries: Array<{freq: number; label: string}> = [\n    {freq: 2, label: '2/wk'},\n    {freq: 1, label: '1/wk'},\n    {freq: 0.5, label: '½/wk'},\n    {freq: 0.25, label: '¼/wk'},\n  ].filter((e) => present.has(e.freq))\n  if (!entries.length) return null\n  return (\n    <span\n      style={{\n        display: 'inline-flex',\n        alignItems: 'center',\n        gap: 8,\n        marginLeft: 'auto',\n      }}\n    >\n      {entries.map((e) => {\n        const [r, g, b] = freqColor(e.freq)\n        return (\n          <span\n            key={e.freq}\n            style={{display: 'inline-flex', alignItems: 'center', gap: 4}}\n          >\n            <span\n              style={{\n                width: 10,\n                height: 10,\n                borderRadius: 5,\n                background: `rgb(${r},${g},${b})`,\n                display: 'inline-block',\n              }}\n            />\n            {e.label}\n          </span>\n        )\n      })}\n    </span>\n  )\n}\n\nfunction normalizeFreq(f: number): number {\n  if (f >= 2) return 2\n  if (f >= 1) return 1\n  if (f >= 0.5) return 0.5\n  if (f > 0) return 0.25\n  return 0\n}\n\nfunction formatWindow(start: string | null, end: string | null): string {"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-07-24T17:31:34.366Z)

Typecheck clean. What you'll see:

- **Route markers only** — the numbered circles on the TSP polyline. Regular POS pins outside the current route keep their existing territory-color scheme, untouched.
- **Color scale** (warmer = more visits per week):
  - **red** = 2/wk
  - **orange** = 1/wk
  - **blue** = 0.5/wk
  - **green** = 0.25/wk
  - grey fallback for anything unrecognized
- **Legend** — appears at the right end of the route-grid header row, and only shows swatches for frequencies actually present on the current day's route (so a single-freq day doesn't render four irrelevant chips).

`updateTriggers` was added on the marker layer's `getFillColor` so deck.gl invalidates its color buffer when a new TSP result comes in.

 "new_string": "/** Slots covered by the current range (or null if no filter is set). */\nexport function rangeSlots(state: DateFilterState): Set<SlotKey> | null {\n  if (state.rangeA === null) return null\n  const b = state.rangeB ?? state.rangeA\n  const lo = Math.min(state.rangeA, b)\n  const hi = Math.max(state.rangeA, b)\n  const out = new Set<SlotKey>()\n  for (let i = lo; i <= hi; i++) {\n    const week = Math.floor(i / 5) + 1\n    const day = (i % 5) + 2\n    out.add(`${week}_${day}` as SlotKey)\n  }\n  return out\n}\n\n/** One entry per day in the current range, in the same order the\n *  operator sees them on the calendar grid. Returns null when no range\n *  is picked (\"All dates\" mode) so callers can distinguish \"explicit\n *  empty\" from \"no selection at all\". */\nexport interface RangeDate {\n  /** YYYY-MM-DD local. Anchors NB job time-windows on the API side. */\n  iso: string\n  /** \"Fri, Aug 7\" — short human label for the tab. */\n  label: string\n  /** Cycle week 1..4. Matches SlotKey's first component. */\n  week: number\n  /** DIAS ATENDIMENTO day code 2..6 (Mon..Fri). */\n  day: number\n  slotKey: SlotKey\n}\n\nexport function enumerateRangeDates(\n  state: DateFilterState,\n): RangeDate[] | null {\n  if (state.rangeA === null) return null\n  const anchor = parseIsoLocal(state.cycleStart)\n  if (!anchor) return null\n  const b = state.rangeB ?? state.rangeA\n  const lo = Math.min(state.rangeA, b)\n  const hi = Math.max(state.rangeA, b)\n  const out: RangeDate[] = []\n  for (let i = lo; i <= hi; i++) {\n    const w = Math.floor(i / 5)\n    const d = i % 5\n    const week = w + 1\n    const day = d + 2\n    // Calendar day = Monday-of-week-1 + (w*7 + d) days. The panel\n    // itself only shows Mon–Fri, so this steps past Sat/Sun cleanly\n    // between weeks — index 5 is Monday of week 2, NOT Saturday.\n    const date = new Date(anchor)\n    date.setDate(date.getDate() + w * 7 + d)\n    out.push({\n      iso: isoLocal(date),\n      label: date.toLocaleDateString(undefined, {\n        weekday: 'short',\n        month: 'short',\n        day: 'numeric',\n      }),\n      week,\n      day,\n      slotKey: `${week}_${day}` as SlotKey,\n    })\n  }\n  return out\n}"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-07-24T17:40:14.565Z)

Typecheck clean. What you'll see:

- **Trigger** — Selecting 1 territory + picking any date range (single day → 20-day full cycle) fires TSPs. "All dates" (no range picked) stays idle, exactly as before, so opening the page never blasts NB.
- **Per-day stop filter** — Each day's TSP only sees POS whose `schedWeeks × schedDays` includes that specific (week, day). So Monday of week 1 gets a different — usually much smaller — stop set than "all POS in the territory".
- **Parallel fetch** — All non-empty days go out at once behind a single `AbortController`, so changing selection cancels everything in flight.
- **Tab bar** — Above the header, one chip per date. Small status dot: amber = loading, green = solved, red = error, grey = < 2 stops today. Scrolls horizontally when the range is long.
- **Map** — Route polyline, numbered stop markers, and text labels update to the active tab only. Switching tabs re-renders the map instantly (data is cached in state).
- **Tab persistence** — Tab stays put when you tweak selection but keeps the same date range; falls back to the first date only when the range changes.

Files touched:
- `apps/route-planner-v2/app/territory-planner/date-filter-panel.tsx` — new `enumerateRangeDates` + `RangeDate` export
- `apps/route-planner-v2/app/territory-planner/territory-map.tsx` — state, fetch, layers, tabbed grid

### CLAUDE (2026-07-31T15:05:19.163Z)

Clean — zero errors in `territory-planner/` files. Typecheck done (bcyd9inw7/bpsg3j4v3 confirmed the fix, b7x0wremg confirmed no regressions in the parent-side plumbing either).

**Summary of the territory-edit feature (net +511 / -29 lines across 2 files + 5 locale JSONs):**

- Click any territory polygon in **hull mode** → "Edit territory N" activates in a new panel next to Boundaries.
- Edit session uses `@nebula.gl` `EditableGeoJsonLayer` + `ModifyMode`: drag vertices, double-click an edge to insert, alt-click to remove. Save/Cancel controls appear during edit.
- Save reassigns POS via `turf.booleanPointInPolygon`: inside the new polygon → new territory; POS displaced from the edited territory → nearest other centroid.
- Downstream (`hullBoundaries`, `visiblePos`, `territoryStats`, per-POS tooltips) reads `effectivePos = stagedPos ?? result.pos`, so the boundary + per-territory counts refresh instantly.
- Sidebar cards for **Max rep-day** and **Hours by weekday** show a small "Stale" chip while edits are pending — those come from the LP solver and need a rebuild to be accurate.
- "Reset" button clears all pending edits and restores the original assignment.

 "old_string": "  const resetEdits = useCallback(() => {\n    setStagedPos(null)\n    setEdit(null)\n    setClickedTerr(null)\n  }, [])",
 "new_string": "  const resetEdits = useCallback(() => {\n    setStagedPos(null)\n    setEdit(null)\n    setClickedTerr(null)\n  }, [])\n\n  // While an edit session is active, disable maplibre's drag-to-pan\n  // handler so mousedown+drag on the map canvas is delivered to\n  // nebula.gl's edit handles instead of starting a pan. Zoom + scroll\n  // stay enabled so the user can still navigate. `dragRotate` is\n  // already off on BaseMap. Re-enable on cleanup so leaving the tab\n  // or hitting Save/Cancel restores normal panning.\n  const {territoryPlannerMap: mapRef} = useMap()\n  useEffect(() => {\n    const raw = mapRef?.getMap?.()\n    if (!raw) return\n    const wasEnabled = raw.dragPan?.isEnabled?.() ?? true\n    if (edit) {\n      raw.dragPan?.disable?.()\n    } else if (!wasEnabled) {\n      raw.dragPan?.enable?.()\n    } else {\n      // Idempotent: ensure it's on when not editing.\n      raw.dragPan?.enable?.()\n    }\n    return () => {\n      // Cleanup always re-enables — protects against unmount mid-edit.\n      raw.dragPan?.enable?.()\n    }\n  }, [edit, mapRef])"
}

### CLAUDE (2026-07-31T15:08:02.095Z)

Typecheck running. While it does, quick note on the fix:

- `useMap()` (from react-map-gl) grabs the `territoryPlannerMap` ref exposed by `<BaseMap mapId="territoryPlannerMap">`.
- When `edit !== null`, we call `map.dragPan.disable()` so mousedown-drag on the canvas no longer starts a map pan — the event drops through to nebula.gl's vertex handles.
- Cleanup always re-enables, so unmount / Cancel / Save all restore panning.
- Zoom and scroll stay on so the user can still navigate to reach vertices.

{
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/libs/territory-planner/src/reschedule.js",
 "content": "'use strict';\n\nconst {parseBase} = require('./parse');\nconst {recomputeTravel} = require('./cluster');\nconst {scheduleAll} = require('./schedule');\nconst {validate} = require('./validate');\n\n/**\n * Re-run scheduling + validation against a client-supplied territory\n * assignment. Skips clustering (buildTerritories) and boundary\n * generation — the caller keeps its current geometry and just wants\n * fresh solver-derived metrics (max rep-day, hours-by-weekday,\n * slots-over-cap) that reflect the current POS -> territory mapping.\n *\n * @param {string|Buffer|ArrayBuffer} input   xlsx workbook (same source\n *                                            the original pipeline ran on)\n * @param {Map<string, number>|Record<string, number>} terrByMatricula\n *        Current territory index (0-based) for each matricula the\n *        caller still tracks. Rows in the workbook whose matricula\n *        isn't in this map are dropped from the reschedule (the\n *        client may have deselected them upstream).\n * @param {number} R                          Number of territories\n * @param {(msg: string) => void} [onLog]\n * @param {{overrides?: {dailyCapH?: number, speedKmh?: number}}} [options]\n * @returns {Promise<{\n *   pos: Array<object>,\n *   R: number,\n *   metrics: object,\n *   slotLoads: number[][][],\n *   dropped: number,\n * }>}\n */\nasync function reschedule(input, terrByMatricula, R, onLog, options) {\n  const log = onLog || (() => {});\n  const opts = options || {};\n  const overrides = opts.overrides || {};\n\n  const terrMap =\n    terrByMatricula instanceof Map\n      ? terrByMatricula\n      : new Map(Object.entries(terrByMatricula || {}).map(([k, v]) => [String(k), Number(v)]));\n\n  log('[1/4] Re-parsing input workbook...');\n  const parsed = await parseBase(input);\n  let pos = parsed.pos;\n\n  // Apply the caller's current assignment. Anything the caller isn't\n  // tracking (e.g. rows they deselected before the original build) is\n  // dropped — including it in the reschedule would inflate metrics.\n  const kept = [];\n  let dropped = 0;\n  for (const p of pos) {\n    const key = String(p.matricula);\n    if (terrMap.has(key)) {\n      p.terr = terrMap.get(key);\n      kept.push(p);\n    } else {\n      dropped++;\n    }\n  }\n  pos = kept;\n  log(`  ${pos.length} POS kept · ${dropped} dropped (not in current assignment)`);\n  if (pos.length < 3) {\n    throw new Error(\n      `Not enough POS to reschedule (${pos.length}). ` +\n      'The current assignment is missing most of the workbook.',\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Reassignment changed each territory's spatial footprint, so the\n  // BHH travel-time estimate has to be redone. `undefined` circuity\n  // falls back to CFG.CIRCUITY — same behaviour as an initial run\n  // without a DM API key, which is what the client can afford here\n  // (no per-territory DM calls at edit time).\n  log('[2/4] Recomputing travel times for new territories...');\n  recomputeTravel(pos, R, undefined, overrides.speedKmh);\n\n  log('[3/4] Rescheduling visit days/weeks (per-territory MILP)...');\n  const slotLoads = await scheduleAll(pos, R, log, {dailyCapH: overrides.dailyCapH});\n\n  log('[4/4] Validating solution...');\n  const {ok, errors, metrics} = validate(pos, R, slotLoads, {\n    dailyCapH: overrides.dailyCapH,\n  });\n  if (!ok) {\n    const preview = errors.slice(0, 20).join('\\n  ');\n    throw new Error(`Reschedule validation failed:\\n  ${preview}`);\n  }\n  log(\n    `  OK - max rep-day ${metrics.maxSlotH} h ` +\n      `(cap ${metrics.dailyCapH} h), 0 violations`,\n  );\n\n  return {pos, R, metrics, slotLoads, dropped};\n}\n\nmodule.exports = {reschedule};\n"
}

The returned `pos` array carries fresh\n// schedDays/schedWeeks from the re-solve.\n\nimport {reschedule, type TerritoryRescheduleOverrides} from '@ncc/territory-planner'\n\nexport const runtime = Response.json(\n          {error: '\"assignments\" must be a JSON object {matricula: terrIndex}'},\n          {status: 400},\n        )\n      }\n    }\n    const ov = form.get('overrides')\n    if JSON object'},\n          {status: 400},\n        )\n      }\n    }\n  } catch {\n    return Response.json({error: 'invalid multipart body'}, {status: 400})\n  }\n  if (!file) {\n    return } finally {\n        controller.close()\n      }\n    },\n  })\n\n  return new Response(stream, {\n    status: 200,\n    headers: {\n      'Content-Type': 'application/x-ndjson; charset=utf-8',\n raw !== 'object') return undefined\n  const src = raw as Record<string, unknown>\n  const out: TerritoryRescheduleOverrides = {}\n  const positive = (v: unknown) =>\n    typeof v === 'number' && Number.isFinite(v) && v > 0 ? v : undefined\n  const daily = positive(src.dailyCapH)\n  const speed = positive(src.speedKmh)\n  if (daily !== undefined) out.dailyCapH = daily\n  if (speed !== Number(p.tempoH.toFixed(3)),\n      visitH: Number(p.visitH.toFixed(3)),\n      weekH: Number(p.weekH.toFixed(3)),\n      schedDays: p.schedDays,\n      schedWeeks: p.schedWeeks,\n      tipo: ### CLAUDE (2026-07-31T15:25:06.478Z)

Waiting on typecheck. Summary of what's now in place:

**Server:**
- `libs/territory-planner/src/cluster.js` — exports `recomputeTravel`
- `libs/territory-planner/src/reschedule.js` (new) — re-parses workbook, applies caller's terr map by matricula, runs `recomputeTravel` (so travel-time is refreshed against new footprints) + `scheduleAll` + `validate`. Skips clustering + boundary generation.
- `libs/territory-planner/src/index.ts` — exports `reschedule`, `TerritoryRescheduleResult`, `TerritoryRescheduleOverrides`
- `apps/route-planner-v2/app/api/territory-planner/reschedule/route.ts` (new) — streaming NDJSON endpoint mirroring the existing pipeline route's shape

**Client (`MapPanel`):**
- Accepts `sourceFile` + `overrides` from parent
- `localResult` state that overlays a rescheduled result on top of `initialResult` (cleared when parent supplies a new solve)
- Reschedule button appears only when there are pending edits, disabled when the source workbook is unavailable (older saved plans)
- Streams the NDJSON response and shows step progress
- On success: replaces metrics + POS in `localResult` (keeps client's current boundaries), clears the stale state so badges disappear

### CLAUDE (2026-07-31T15:32:19.634Z)

While that runs — the fix in plain terms:

- Previously: `MapPanel.onSave` was `() => void`, so the parent's `confirmSave` had no way to know about local edits and always persisted `phase.result` (the untouched pipeline output).
- Now: `onSave(effectiveResult)` — MapPanel computes the current effective snapshot:
  - `localResult` if a Recalculate has run (fresh metrics + fresh POS schedules)
  - `{...initialResult, pos: editedPos}` if edits are pending but Recalculate hasn't run (still stale metrics, but pos.terr reflects the edits)
  - `initialResult` if untouched
- Parent stashes that snapshot in `saveDialog.result`, then `confirmSave` writes it to storage instead of `phase.result`.
- Additionally: `setPhase(...)` now replaces `phase.result` with the saved snapshot so the sidebar's own numbers match what was persisted (no more divergence between "what's saved" and "what's shown"). Boundaries carry through from `initialResult` — hulls are recomputed from `pos.terr` when the plan is reopened, so the edited layout renders on reload.

 "new_string": "/** Independent post-solve checks. Returns {ok, errors, metrics}.\n *  `options.dailyCapH` overrides CFG.DAILY_CAP_H for the over-cap check\n *  and the reported metric so downstream UI matches the run's config.\n *  `options.allowOverCap` — when true, slots exceeding the daily cap\n *  populate metrics.slotsOverCap as usual but DON'T fail validation.\n *  Useful for post-edit reschedules where a user has intentionally\n *  overloaded a territory and just wants to see the resulting numbers\n *  rather than a hard blocker. Other checks (day feasibility,\n *  restricted days, visit-count shape) still enforce. */\nfunction validate(pos, R, slotLoads, options = {}) {\n  const dailyCap = options.dailyCapH ?? CFG.DAILY_CAP_H;\n  const allowOverCap = options.allowOverCap === true;\n  const errors = [];\n  for (const p of pos) {\n    const ds = p.schedDays, ws = p.schedWeeks;\n    if (!ds.every((d) => p.eff.has(d))) errors.push(`${p.matricula}: day not allowed`);\n    if (ds.some((d) => p.restr.has(d))) errors.push(`${p.matricula}: restricted day`);\n    if (ds.length * ws.length !== Math.round(p.freq * 4)) errors.push(`${p.matricula}: visit count`);\n    const wkey = ws.join(',');\n    if (p.freq === 2 && (ds.length !== 2 || wkey !== '1,2,3,4')) errors.push(`${p.matricula}: freq2 shape`);\n    if (p.freq === 1 && (ds.length !== 1 || wkey !== '1,2,3,4')) errors.push(`${p.matricula}: freq1 shape`);\n    if (p.freq === 0.5 && (ds.length !== 1 || (wkey !== '1,3' && wkey !== '2,4'))) errors.push(`${p.matricula}: freq0.5 shape`);\n    if (p.freq === 0.25 && (ds.length !== 1 || ws.length !== 1)) errors.push(`${p.matricula}: freq0.25 shape`);\n  }\n  const flat = slotLoads.flat(2);\n  const overCap = flat.filter((v) => v > dailyCap + 1e-6).length;\n  if (overCap && !allowOverCap) errors.push(`${overCap} rep-day slots exceed daily capacity`);"

{

 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/apps/route-planner-v2/app/territory-planner/client.tsx",
 "old_string": "  // What Save persists. Priority: localResult (post-Recalculate — has\n  // fresh metrics + schedules) → editedPos overlay on initialResult\n  // (edits pending, metrics still stale) → initialResult untouched.\n  // Boundaries always carry through from initialResult; hulls redraw\n  // client-side from pos.terr when the plan is reopened.\n  const effectiveResultForSave = useMemo<TerritoryResult>(() => {\n    if (localResult) return localResult\n    if (editedPos) return {...initialResult, pos: editedPos}\n    return initialResult\n  }, [localResult, editedPos, initialResult])",
 "new_string": "  // What Save persists. Priority: localResult (post-Recalculate — has\n  // fresh metrics + schedules) → editedPos overlay on initialResult\n  // (edits pending, metrics still stale) → initialResult untouched.\n  // Boundaries always carry through from initialResult; hulls redraw\n  // client-side from pos.terr when the plan is reopened.\n  const effectiveResultForSave = useMemo<TerritoryResult>(() => {\n    if (localResult) return localResult\n    if (editedPos) return {...initialResult, pos: editedPos}\n    return initialResult\n  }, [localResult, editedPos, initialResult])\n\n  // Per-territory table. Reconstructs slot loads from pos.schedDays /\n  // schedWeeks / visitH — no server round-trip needed. In state 2\n  // (edits committed but not recalculated) each moved POS carries its\n  // OLD schedule into its NEW territory, so maxRepDayH is an\n  // approximation that gets a stale badge until Recalculate runs.\n  const territoryTable = useMemo(() => {\n    const pos = effectiveResultForSave.pos\n    // 5 weekdays (Mon..Fri) × 4 weeks. FEMSA day codes: 2..6.\n    // Zero-init per territory so empty territories still render.\n    const loads: number[][][] = Array.from({length: result.R}, () =>\n      Array.from({length: 4}, () => [0, 0, 0, 0, 0]),\n    )\n    const rows = Array.from({length: result.R}, (_, t) => ({\n      terr: t,\n      count: 0,\n      visits: 0,\n      weekH: 0,\n      serviceH: 0,\n      maxSlotH: 0,\n    }))\n    for (const p of pos) {\n      if (p.terr < 0 || p.terr >= result.R) continue\n      const row = rows[p.terr]\n      row.count += 1\n      row.weekH += p.weekH\n      row.serviceH += p.freq * p.tempoH\n      row.visits += Math.round(p.freq * 4)\n      const terrLoads = loads[p.terr]\n      for (const w of p.schedWeeks) {\n        for (const d of p.schedDays) {\n          const wi = w - 1\n          const di = d - 2\n          if (wi >= 0 && wi < 4 && di >= 0 && di < 5) {\n            terrLoads[wi][di] += p.visitH\n          }\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    for (let t = 0; t < result.R; t++) {\n      let mx = 0\n      for (const week of loads[t]) for (const v of week) if (v > mx) mx = v\n      rows[t].maxSlotH = mx\n    }\n    return rows\n  }, [effectiveResultForSave.pos, result.R])"
}

  'pl-PL': {'colLat': 'Szerokość', 'colLon': 'Długość'},

}
for loc, keys in translations.items():
    path = f'apps/route-planner-v2/messages/{loc}.json'
    with open(path) as f:
        d = json.load(f)
    tp = d.setdefault('territoryPlanner', {})

            tp[k] = v
    with open(path, 'w') as f:
        json.dump(d, f, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
        f.write('\n')
    print(loc, 'ok')
PY

### CLAUDE (2026-07-31T16:56:44.102Z)

Waiting on typecheck (bo5irss5d). What this adds:

- Right-click a POS pin → context menu appears at cursor with a red "Delete POS" item
- Right-clicking empty map or a boundary shows the native menu (unchanged)
- Click Delete → confirmation dialog with the POS matricula + territory number
- Confirm → POS is removed from `stagedPos` (client-side overlay), which:
  - Immediately drops it from the map (hull, POS layer, territory stats table update via the existing `effectivePos` chain)
  - Emits `onEditedPos(stagedPos)` to the parent → Max rep-day + Hours-by-weekday get their "Stale" badges → Recalculate panel appears
- Recalculate already handles this cleanly: the reschedule endpoint filters the workbook to matriculas present in `assignments`, so deleted POS are dropped from the server-side re-solve too (they show up in the `dropped` counter in the response log)
- Cancels any in-flight boundary edit — the working ring might reference the deleted POS

### USER (2026-07-31T17:27:30.839Z)

is the 'rescheduling' of a stale solution performed server-side or is it client-side


### CLAUDE (2026-07-31T17:27:46.796Z)

Server-side.

The **Recalculate** button POSTs to `/route-planner/api/territory-planner/reschedule` (server route in `apps/route-planner-v2/app/api/territory-planner/reschedule/route.ts`). That route calls `reschedule()` in `libs/territory-planner/src/reschedule.js`, which runs on the Node runtime and:

1. Re-parses the workbook (`parseBase`) — needs the server-only `patterns` / `eff` / `restr` fields that don't survive the client's serialized POS shape
2. Applies the client's current `matricula → terr` assignments
3. `recomputeTravel()` — refreshes BHH travel time for the new footprints
4. `scheduleAll()` — the per-territory MILP (HiGHS WASM, uses `libs/territory-planner/src/lp.js`)
5. `validate()` — with `allowOverCap` toggle from the checkbox
6. `buildBoundaries()` — rebuilds voronoi against the reassigned POS

The endpoint streams NDJSON progress (`type: 'log'`) as each step completes; the client renders those inline in the Recalculate panel.

**What's client-side** (no network):
- The territory-boundary edit itself (nebula.gl vertex drag + `applyEdit` point-in-polygon reassign)
- POS delete (right-click)
- Approximated per-territory stats + calendar-view slot loads (reconstructed from `pos.schedDays / schedWeeks / visitH`)
- Hull recomputation

Client-side stays snappy for edits; the LP scheduler stays on the server because HiGHS + the shared solver code aren't in the browser bundle.

CFG.DAILY_CAP_H;\n  const sub = pos.filter((p) => p.terr === terr);\n  // spatial day-sectors: 5 centroids ordered by angle around territory center\n  const km = kmeans(sub.map((p) => ({ x: p.x, y: p.y, w: p.weekH })), 5, { seed: 7 });",
 "new_string": "/** Per-territory MILP: pick one (days, weeks) pattern per POS to minimize the max\n *  (week, day) slot load, with a small spatial-affinity tiebreak.\n *  `dailyCap` — effective daily capacity in hours (falls back to CFG). */\nasync function scheduleTerritory(pos, terr, log, dailyCap) {\n  const cap = dailyCap ?? CFG.DAILY_CAP_H;\n  const sub = pos.filter((p) => p.terr === terr);\n  // Empty territory — can happen when a boundary edit reassigns every\n  // POS out of a terr. Nothing to schedule; return all-zero slot loads\n  // so downstream (scheduleAll → validate) sees a well-formed result\n  // rather than tripping on kmeans([]) or reducing over `sub.map(p =>\n  // p.x)`.\n  if (sub.length === 0) {\n    const emptyLoads = {};\n    for (const w of CFG.WEEKS) for (const d of CFG.DAYS) emptyLoads[`${w}_${d}`] = 0;\n    return { status: 'Empty', loads: emptyLoads };\n  }\n  // spatial day-sectors: 5 centroids ordered by angle around territory center\n  const km = kmeans(sub.map((p) => ({ x: p.x, y: p.y, w: p.weekH })), 5, { seed: 7 });"

### CLAUDE (2026-07-31T18:27:42.597Z)

OOM — memory limit hit, container killed mid-pipeline, stream closed with no `result` event. That's exactly what you observed.

Fix: bump memory + CPU + timeout on the Cloud Run service. I'll edit `cloud_run.tf` and apply. Values I'll use:

- `memory = "2Gi"` (from 512 MiB) — safe headroom for HiGHS + exceljs + territory data
- `cpu = "2"` (from 1) — LP solver benefits, and Cloud Run requires CPU ≥ 2 for memory > 1 GiB
- `timeout = "900s"` (from 300 s) — 15 min ceiling
- `startup_cpu_boost = true` — helps first-request WASM init

{
 "replace_all": false,
 "file_path": "/Users/[USER]/workspace/ncc/libs/territory-planner/src/parse.js",
 "old_string": "/** Read the Base sheet -> array of POS records (active only) + excluded count.\n *  `input` may be a file path (string) or an in-memory Buffer/ArrayBuffer. */\nasync function parseBase(input) {\n  const wb = new ExcelJS.Workbook();\n  if (typeof input === 'string') {\n    await wb.xlsx.readFile(input);\n  } else if (input && typeof input === 'object' && 'byteLength' in input) {\n    // Buffer or ArrayBuffer — exceljs load() expects a Buffer.\n    const buf = Buffer.isBuffer(input) ? input : Buffer.from(input);\n    await wb.xlsx.load(buf);\n  } else {\n    throw new Error('parseBase: expected a file path or Buffer/ArrayBuffer');\n  }\n  const ws = wb.getWorksheet('Base') || wb.worksheets[0];",
 "new_string": "/** True when `buf` looks like a ZIP-based XLSX (starts with the PK\n *  signature). Anything else — a path with .csv, a raw text buffer —\n *  is treated as CSV. Cheap sniff; avoids requiring the caller to pass\n *  a content-type or extension. */\nfunction looksLikeXlsx(buf) {\n  return buf.length >= 2 && buf[0] === 0x50 && buf[1] === 0x4b;\n}\n\n/** Read a CSV Buffer into an exceljs workbook. Uses a Readable stream\n *  because exceljs's csv reader accepts streams (or file paths) but\n *  not raw buffers. The resulting workbook has a single worksheet\n *  which the rest of parseBase picks up via `wb.worksheets[0]`. */\nasync function loadCsvBuffer(wb, buf) {\n  const {Readable} = require('stream');\n  const stream = Readable.from(buf);\n  await wb.csv.read(stream);\n}\n\n/** Read the Base sheet -> array of POS records (active only) + excluded count.\n *  `input` may be a file path (string, .xlsx or .csv) or an in-memory\n *  Buffer/ArrayBuffer. Format is auto-detected by content sniff. */\nasync function parseBase(input) {\n  const wb = new ExcelJS.Workbook();\n  if (typeof input === 'string') {\n    // File path — extension picks the reader.\n    if (/\\.csv$/i.test(input)) {\n      await wb.csv.readFile(input);\n    } else {\n      await wb.xlsx.readFile(input);\n    }\n  } else if (input && typeof input === 'object' && 'byteLength' in input) {\n    // Buffer or ArrayBuffer — exceljs load() expects a Buffer.\n    const buf = Buffer.isBuffer(input) ? input : Buffer.from(input);\n    if (looksLikeXlsx(buf)) {\n      await wb.xlsx.load(buf);\n    } else {\n      await loadCsvBuffer(wb, buf);\n    }\n  } else {\n    throw new Error('parseBase: expected a file path or Buffer/ArrayBuffer');\n  }\n  const ws = wb.getWorksheet('Base') || wb.worksheets[0];"
